headline: Asia-Pacific braces for the world's steepest medical cost inflation
summary: A global WTW survey of insurers found APAC medical costs are expected to climb about 14% in 2026 (nearly 17% in Singapore), led by cancer and cardiovascular claims, with most insurers expecting elevated cost trends to persist for years.

headline: TPA and claims-services deal flow set to keep accelerating as PE holders near exit windows
summary: MarshBerry's analysis finds consolidation among TPAs and claims-services firms still accelerating, with private equity sponsors' lengthening hold periods pointing toward more recapitalizations, secondary sales and bolt-on deals ahead.

headline: Bupa reshuffles top leadership across its UK, India and European units
summary: Bupa named Chris Carroll to lead its Global, India and UK business while his predecessor Carlos Jaureguizar moves to head Bupa's Europe and Latin America division, part of a broader senior leadership shake-up effective January 2026.

headline: SECURE 2.0's Roth catch-up contribution mandate takes effect for higher earners
summary: Starting January 1, 2026, SECURE 2.0 requires employees age 50-plus earning more than $150,000 in FICA wages to make catch-up 401(k) contributions on a Roth, after-tax basis, a compliance change employers spent the year preparing payroll and plan systems for.

headline: Fitch keeps APAC insurance outlook neutral for 2026 despite rising claims costs
summary: Fitch Ratings maintained a neutral 2026 outlook for Asia-Pacific insurers, citing capital buffers and disciplined underwriting offsetting rising claims costs, with non-life premium growth forecast at 2.5%.

headline: Stanford-Harvard report finds clinical AI hype colliding with real-world limits
summary: A joint Stanford-Harvard 'State of Clinical AI' report examines which AI tools are actually delivering value inside hospitals after a boom in pilots, highlighting gaps between vendor promises and clinical performance.

headline: Pension risk transfer buy-ins hit record as plan sponsors de-risk
summary: US pension buy-in transactions reached roughly $17.5 billion across 17 deals in 2025 as the structure moved from a niche tool for mega-plans to a mainstream de-risking step, part of an overall $48.7 billion pension risk transfer market tracked by Aon.

headline: UK's PRA to review insurers' handling of solvency-triggered bulk annuity termination clauses
summary: The Prudential Regulation Authority plans in 2026 to revisit how bulk purchase annuity writers responded to its 2025 Dear CEO letter on solvency-triggered termination rights, part of a broader regulatory focus on the fast-growing pension risk transfer market.

headline: Global Property Catastrophe Reinsurance Rates Post Steepest Drop Since 2014
summary: Risk-adjusted global property catastrophe reinsurance rates fell an average of 14.7% at the January 2026 renewals, the sharpest year-on-year decline since 2014, as record capital inflows and strong ILS issuance pushed the market into a buyer-favorable cycle.

headline: Self-funded employers head into 2026 squeezed by rising stop-loss costs and thinner TPA margins
summary: A strategic outlook on self-funded healthcare warns that rising stop-loss premiums, growing pharmacy complexity and heavier regulatory scrutiny are converging to pressure both employers and the TPAs that administer their plans in 2026.

headline: Supreme Court to weigh benchmark standard in 401(k) fee lawsuits
summary: The US Supreme Court agreed to hear Anderson v. Intel, a case that will decide whether ERISA fiduciary-breach claims over fund underperformance must point to a 'meaningful benchmark,' with a ruling likely to shape litigation risk just as regulators open the door to alternative investments in plans.

headline: APG Asset Management's chief executive to depart after two decades
summary: Ronald Wuijster is stepping down as CEO of Dutch pension investor APG Asset Management, with an interim successor taking over responsibilities from March 2026 pending regulatory approval, marking the end of a near 20-year tenure.

headline: Cloud security startup Upwind reaches unicorn status with $250 million Series B
summary: Upwind raised a $250 million Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners at a $1.5 billion valuation, bringing total funding to $430 million as it scales runtime-first cloud security tools relevant to financial-services risk teams.

headline: WTW completes $1.3 billion acquisition of tech-enabled broker Newfront
summary: Willis Towers Watson finalized its purchase of Newfront Insurance Holdings for $1.3 billion, adding the San Francisco-based broker's technology-driven middle-market and specialty business to its Risk & Broking and Health, Wealth & Career units.

headline: UnitedHealth pours $1.5 billion into AI to chase $1 billion in savings
summary: UnitedHealthcare's CEO said the insurer expects nearly $1 billion in AI-enabled operating cost reductions in 2026, backed by a $1.5 billion technology investment aimed at automating claims processing and member service through Optum.

headline: DOL proposes first federal fee-disclosure rule targeting PBMs and TPAs
summary: The US Department of Labor proposed a rule that would require pharmacy benefit managers and third-party administrators to give employer-sponsored ERISA health plans detailed advance disclosure of the fees they charge.

headline: DOL's proposed PBM fee-disclosure rule set to reach TPAs for plan years starting July 2026
summary: A Department of Labor proposal would force pharmacy benefit managers and the TPAs and insurers that administer PBM services for self-funded ERISA health plans to make detailed compensation disclosures, with applicability proposed for plan years beginning on or after July 1, 2026.
source_name: U.S. Department of Labor / Federal Register

headline: US insurtechs pull in $420 million in January as mega-rounds return
summary: Global insurtech funding rebounded to roughly $420 million in January 2026, driven largely by a handful of large US-based deals, according to Fintech Global's tracking data.

headline: Congress enacts PBM reforms delinking Medicare Part D compensation from drug prices
summary: New federal legislation delinks pharmacy benefit manager compensation from drug prices in Medicare Part D, shifting to flat 'bona fide service fees' and prohibiting Medicaid spread pricing under a pass-through model.

headline: India's health insurance premiums surge nearly 27% as GST cut and government schemes drive volume
summary: Health insurance gross written premiums in India jumped sharply at the start of 2026, helped by a GST reduction on retail policies and expanded enrollment in government schemes such as Ayushman Bharat.

headline: Brookfield Asset Management installs Connor Teskey as CEO
summary: Brookfield Asset Management named Connor Teskey chief executive effective February 2026, with longtime leader Bruce Flatt stepping back to chair the board and continuing as CEO of parent Brookfield Corporation.

headline: New federal law widens fee-disclosure duties to TPAs and stop-loss insurers
summary: The Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026 expanded compensation-disclosure obligations beyond pharmacy benefit managers to cover third-party administrators, stop-loss insurers and most other group health plan service providers, with penalties up to $10,000 a day for noncompliance.

headline: Congress's PBM reform law starts reshaping drug-pricing transparency
summary: The Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026 codified sweeping pharmacy benefit manager reforms, requiring semiannual disclosure of net drug spending and rebates to employer plans and phasing in bans on rebate-linked PBM compensation by 2028.

headline: FTC secures landmark Express Scripts settlement expected to cut insulin costs by billions
summary: The FTC settled its insulin-pricing lawsuit against Express Scripts, forcing the PBM to stop favoring high-list-price drugs on formularies, delink compensation from negotiated savings, and boost transparency — changes projected to save patients up to $7 billion over a decade.

headline: Blue Ridge Associates grows ESOP administration arm by buying AmbroseAdvisors' TPA unit
summary: Blue Ridge Associates acquired the ESOP third-party administration services business of AmbroseAdvisors, broadening its retirement-plan TPA footprint.

headline: Medi Assist Completes Takeover of Paramount's TPA Business in India
summary: Medi Assist Insurance TPA finished absorbing rival Paramount Health Services' licensed third-party administrator operations via a slump-sale transfer, cementing its position as India's largest TPA and unifying claims servicing across both books.

headline: Australia approves near-4.5% private health insurance premium hike
summary: Australia's government signed off on an average 4.41% increase to private health insurance premiums from April 2026, citing rising hospital and medical service costs, while continuing to fund a multi-billion-dollar policyholder rebate.
source_name: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing

headline: Congress enacts sweeping PBM reform bill delinking pay from drug prices
summary: New federal legislation passed in early 2026 bars PBMs from earning compensation tied to drug prices or rebates in Medicare Part D starting 2028, bans Medicaid spread pricing, and adds annual data-transparency requirements to HHS.

headline: Fiduciary Services Group snaps up another New England retirement-plan TPA
summary: Fiduciary Services Group acquired Vermont-based Future Planning Associates, its third TPA/recordkeeping bolt-on in about 14 months, as it continues rolling smaller administrators into its national platform.

headline: Jointly AI launches autonomous AI broker platform for UK personal lines
summary: Jointly AI introduced what it calls the first end-to-end autonomous AI insurance brokerage platform for UK personal lines, using voice AI agents to contact insurers, gather quotes and return recommendations without manual broker intervention.

headline: UK bulk annuity market on pace for record £70 billion in 2026
summary: The Association of British Insurers has stood up a new pensions board to focus on defined-benefit risk transfer and bulk annuity activity, as total UK pension risk transferred to insurers is projected to climb roughly 15% this year with more large scheme deals expected.

headline: New law expands compensation-disclosure duties to TPAs and stop-loss carriers
summary: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 extends compensation-disclosure requirements beyond brokers to third-party administrators, PBMs, stop-loss carriers and other group-health-plan vendors, requiring disclosure of direct and indirect compensation before contracts take effect, with penalties up to $10,000 per day for noncompliance.

headline: UK's FCA lays out 2026 insurance supervision priorities in first annual report
summary: The Financial Conduct Authority published its first annual insurance-sector regulatory priorities report, consolidating prior portfolio letters and putting claims handling and access to insurance for vulnerable consumers at the center.

headline: Cytora launches Autopilot, an end-to-end automated commercial underwriting platform
summary: Cytora launched Autopilot, described as the first end-to-end AI-automated underwriting platform for commercial insurance, aiming to run entire underwriting workflows with minimal manual intervention.

headline: Cigna hands CEO reins to longtime insider Brian Evanko
summary: After a multi-year succession process, Cigna's president and COO Brian Evanko took over as chief executive on July 1, 2026, with predecessor David Cordani moving into the executive chair role.

headline: Singapore refreshes AI-in-healthcare guidelines with bias and performance monitoring rules
summary: Singapore's Ministry of Health and Health Sciences Authority published updated AI in Healthcare Guidelines requiring ongoing validation, performance monitoring and bias detection for clinical AI tools deployed in the city-state.

headline: PBM giant MedImpact bulks up its risk-management arm with two acquisitions
summary: MedImpact, one of the largest independent U.S. pharmacy benefit managers, acquired two employer stop-loss and risk-management firms to broaden its offerings for self-funded employer health plans.

headline: PartnerRe Names New CEO for Its Americas P&C Business
summary: PartnerRe appointed Scott Kreuzer, a nearly 30-year reinsurance veteran most recently of Aspen Insurance Group, as CEO of its P&C Americas division, succeeding Jon Colello who moved into a president role.

headline: Willis and Qover team up to expand embedded-insurance offering across industries
summary: Broking giant Willis and Belgian insurtech Qover launched a partnership widening the GB Affinity ecosystem, aiming to give businesses a fast, product-agnostic way to launch point-of-sale insurance programs at scale.

headline: Corebridge and Equitable agree to $22 billion all-stock merger
summary: Corebridge Financial and Equitable Holdings will combine in an all-stock deal valued near $22 billion, creating a combined retirement, life insurance and asset management platform with roughly $1.5 trillion in assets under management and administration. The merged company will operate under the Equitable name and trade under ticker EQH, with closing expected by year-end 2026.

headline: India's Plum raises $20 million to scale its corporate health-insurance platform
summary: Bengaluru-based employee health-benefits startup Plum raised about ₹193 crore ($20.6M) in a Series B led by Peak XV Partners to expand its claims platform, AI-driven processing, and preventive-care services across its 600,000-plus covered lives.

headline: Employee-benefits insurtech Plum raises ₹193 crore after turning profitable
summary: Indian B2B health-benefits platform Plum raised about $20.6 million in a Series B led by Peak XV Partners, nearly doubling its valuation, to invest in AI-driven claims operations and deepen HR and payroll integrations.

headline: Corebridge and Equitable combine in $22 billion deal to build a $1.5 trillion retirement giant
summary: Corebridge Financial and Equitable Holdings agreed to an all-stock merger that would create the largest annuity seller in the country by volume, serving more than 12 million customers with a combined $1.5 trillion in assets once the deal closes by year-end 2026.

headline: DOL proposes safe harbor clearing path for private assets in 401(k)s
summary: The Department of Labor proposed a process-based safe harbor under ERISA that would give plan fiduciaries a clearer, presumption-of-prudence route to include alternative investments such as private equity, real estate and infrastructure in participant-directed retirement plan lineups.

headline: India forces life insurers onto new accounting standard, upending reported earnings
summary: IRDAI's board approved changes requiring life insurers to switch to Ind AS-based financial statements starting April 2026, a shift expected to significantly alter how carriers recognize and disclose profits and reserves.

headline: DOL fiduciary safe harbor could open 401(k) menus to private equity
summary: Following President Trump's 2025 executive order, the Department of Labor advanced a proposed six-factor safe harbor letting plan fiduciaries add private equity, private credit and other alternatives to 401(k) lineups without automatically inviting litigation risk, potentially touching over 90 million DC savers.

headline: DOL retirement-advice fiduciary rule officially vacated for a second time
summary: The Department of Labor's 2024 Retirement Security Rule defining an investment advice fiduciary was formally removed effective April 20, 2026, reverting to the 1975 five-part test, with a Trump-era replacement rule possibly coming as soon as May 2026.

headline: Wearable maker Whoop triples its valuation to $10 billion ahead of an IPO
summary: Fitness-tracking company Whoop raised $575 million in a Series G round backed by sovereign wealth funds and celebrity investors, tripling its valuation as its CEO signaled an IPO is the company's next step.

headline: North American Risk Services Names New Workers' Comp Chief
summary: Claims and TPA firm North American Risk Services has appointed industry veteran Alice Wells to head its workers' compensation division, tasking her with overseeing claims strategy and operations nationwide.

headline: Japan, Korea and India reinsurance buyers lock in double-digit rate cuts at April renewals
summary: Ample capacity and a stretch of relatively low catastrophe activity gave Asia-Pacific cedents strong leverage at the April 1 renewal, with global reinsurance demand also climbing about 10% as buyers sought broader protection.

headline: Acrisure completes acquisition of technology-driven property MGA Vave from Canopius
summary: Acrisure finalized its purchase of Vave, Canopius Group's technology-driven property managing general agent, expanding Acrisure's specialty MGA distribution footprint.

headline: Cara pulls in $8 million seed round to automate brokerage back-office work
summary: The AI platform for insurance brokerages, backed by Stripe's former COO and other tech veterans, says it reached seven-figure annual revenue within seven months by automating proposals, certificates and client communications.

headline: Singapore Tightens Rules on Private Health Insurance Riders to Curb Cost Spiral
summary: Singapore's Ministry of Health introduced new requirements for Integrated Shield Plan riders, including higher mandatory co-payments, aimed at reining in rapidly rising private healthcare costs. The changes are expected to lower new rider premiums by roughly 30% as medical inflation in the country is projected near 17% this year.

headline: Acrisure Folds Tech-First Property MGA Vave Into Its Underwriting Platform
summary: Acrisure completed its acquisition of Vave, a data-driven excess-and-surplus property MGA that issues over 10,000 automated quotes daily, from Canopius Group, adding it to Acrisure Underwriting's roster of a dozen MGAs.

headline: Old Republic spins up Lodestar Claims & Risk Services as standalone TPA brand
summary: Old Republic International launched Lodestar Claims & Risk Services as an independent operating company and brand within the group, its first such standalone TPA launch in more than 30 years.

headline: Acrisure Bolts On Four UK Brokers and an MGA in Specialist Push
summary: Acrisure's UK broking arm acquired retail brokers Heathwoods, Marrs and Smith Greenfield along with London MGA Confidas, broadening its commercial, property, high-net-worth and heritage-risk capabilities amid continued UK broker consolidation.

headline: AI Broker Startup Rosella Raises Early Funding From Peak XV, Intact
summary: Indian AI-powered commercial insurance broker Rosella closed a $2.6 million round led by Peak XV Partners and Intact Private Capital to automate policy comparison and quoting workflows for construction, manufacturing and logistics SMEs.

headline: Health-plan infrastructure startup Yuzu Health lands $35 million to modernize TPA operations
summary: Yuzu Health closed a Series A led by General Catalyst and Chemistry to expand its platform for claims processing, eligibility and stop-loss administration, having already processed over $1 billion in claims across all 50 states.

headline: MSIG Asia recruits QBE veteran Ronak Shah to lead its regional business
summary: Singapore-based insurer MSIG Asia named Ronak Shah, formerly CEO of QBE's Wholesale Markets Asia, as its new Regional CEO effective October 2026, giving him oversight of operations spanning Southeast Asia, Hong Kong, India, Oceania and Greater China.

headline: Manulife taps Brett Marchand to lead its wealth arm after abrupt exit of predecessor
summary: Manulife Wealth & Asset Management named longtime executive Brett Marchand as president and CEO of Manulife Wealth after Richard McIntyre departed for another opportunity, alongside other Canada retirement leadership moves.

headline: Manulife Wealth names new president and CEO in leadership shake-up
summary: Manulife Wealth & Asset Management said Brett Marchand will become president and CEO of Manulife Wealth, succeeding Richard McIntyre, as part of a broader round of leadership changes across its wealth and retirement businesses.

headline: Trucking insurance brokerage buys its AI automation vendor outright, launches Insure Stack
summary: After using Mulligan to automate up to 90% of manual quoting and proposal work, Prestige Trucking Insurance acquired the AI platform from Pyq and relaunched it as a standalone company, Insure Stack, to sell the technology to other brokerages.

headline: Asia-Pacific's MGA boom shifts from land-grab growth to disciplined scale
summary: Guy Carpenter's regional MGA lead says Asia-Pacific managing general agents are moving away from rapid, growth-at-all-costs expansion toward tighter underwriting discipline and greater use of technology, as third-party capital increasingly favors established platforms with clear profit plans.

headline: Hospital CEO exits jump 32% as long-tenured leaders finally step aside
summary: Hospital and health-system CEO departures rose sharply in early 2026 versus the prior year, with veteran leaders including Mayo Clinic's Gianrico Farrugia and Yale New Haven Health's Christopher O'Connor announcing they are stepping down.

headline: Visa partners with French insurtech Neat to embed insurance in card experiences
summary: Visa and Neat formed a partnership to embed insurance products directly into Visa card experiences, part of a broader industry push to build protection into the payment moment rather than sell it separately.

headline: Visa teams with insurtech Neat to modernize embedded card insurance
summary: Payments giant Visa is partnering with French insurtech Neat to give cardholders clearer coverage information and faster claims resolution as part of a push to embed insurance benefits more seamlessly into card products.

headline: Old Republic Spins Off Claims Unit as Standalone Brand Lodestar
summary: After more than three decades operating inside Old Republic, the insurer's third-party administration business has been relaunched as an independent company, Lodestar Claims & Risk Services, giving the national claims provider its own market identity.

headline: Old Republic spins off Lodestar as independent brand for its TPA business
summary: Old Republic International launched Lodestar Claims & Risk Services as a standalone brand for its third-party administrator operations, the first time in more than 30 years the unit has operated under its own identity while keeping the same claims teams.

headline: Old Republic spins out TPA business as independent brand Lodestar
summary: Old Republic International launched Lodestar Claims & Risk Services as a standalone operating company, the first time in more than 30 years its third-party administrator business has carried its own distinct brand in the market.

headline: BrokerTech Ventures names 2026 accelerator cohort of nine insurtech startups
summary: BrokerTech Ventures selected nine insurtech startups for its 2026 accelerator cohort, each receiving $50,000 in seed funding and access to BTV's broker and carrier distribution network to pilot their technology.

headline: CMS's 2026 Medicare Advantage rule bars retroactive denials, tightens prior-authorization timelines
summary: CMS finalized 2026 Medicare Advantage rules requiring plans to honor prior-authorization decisions, barring retroactive denial of approved services absent fraud, and setting 72-hour and seven-day response deadlines for expedited and standard requests.

headline: Commercial insurance pricing turns negative for brokers for first time since 2017
summary: The Council of Insurance Agents & Brokers reported that average commercial premiums fell 1.2% in Q1 2026 across all account sizes, ending a 33-quarter run of increases, with property rates down sharply while casualty and commercial auto continued to harden.

headline: Commercial insurance pricing falls globally for a seventh straight quarter
summary: Marsh's Global Insurance Market Index shows worldwide commercial rates dropped about 5% in Q1 2026 as abundant capacity and heavy insurer competition pushed pricing down across nearly every region and major product line.

headline: Insurtech investment climbs to $1.63 billion in Q1 2026 as AI dominates deal flow
summary: CB Insights data shows global insurtech investment rose about 27% year-over-year to $1.63 billion in Q1 2026, with AI-branded startups capturing a record 95%-plus share of the capital.

headline: US commercial insurance market splits in two as property rates crater and casualty keeps hardening
summary: Commercial property pricing fell a record 7.1% in the first quarter of 2026 on abundant capacity, while casualty lines including commercial auto kept seeing high-single to double-digit rate increases amid persistent social inflation.

headline: Asia-Pacific digital health investment splits sharply toward infrastructure over startups
summary: Analysis of first-quarter 2026 deal flow found roughly $2.65 billion in strategic digital health investment across Asia-Pacific compared to just $244 million in traditional venture funding, signaling investors are prioritizing healthcare data and AI infrastructure over early-stage startups.

headline: Asset-intensive reinsurance keeps expanding across Asia-Pacific life insurance
summary: Insurers in the region are increasingly using asset-intensive reinsurance and sidecar structures to manage capital under new solvency regimes taking effect in 2026, a trend that is now drawing closer regulatory scrutiny over concentration risk.

headline: Insurance distribution dealmaking slows to its weakest quarterly pace in a decade
summary: Global insurance brokerage and agency M&A volume fell to its lowest first-quarter tally since 2016, though analysts note the three-year decline appears to be leveling off as buyers shift toward smaller tuck-in deals.

headline: Broker deal multiples hold up even as AI casts a shadow over the sector
summary: A 2026 broker M&A outlook finds that while AI-driven disruption fears have added scrutiny to deals and pressured some public broker valuations, well-run agencies and niche MGAs are still commanding strong, in some cases mid-to-high-teens, EBITDA multiples. Analysts expect another active year for brokerage consolidation despite the uncertainty.

headline: Sompo backs UK insurtech Zego with $28 million to build Japanese telematics insurance
summary: Japanese insurer Sompo Holdings invested in a $28 million funding round for UK digital motor insurer Zego, partnering to bring usage-based, telematics-rated motor insurance products to the Japanese market.

headline: UnitedHealth's Q1 medical loss ratio beats expectations, prompting raised guidance
summary: UnitedHealth reported first-quarter 2026 revenue of $111.7 billion and a medical loss ratio of 83.9%, well below analyst expectations, and raised its full-year adjusted earnings guidance on strong medical cost management.

headline: SEC and CFTC move to slash private fund reporting requirements
summary: The two regulators jointly proposed raising Form PF filing thresholds, eliminating quarterly private-equity event reporting, and easing hedge fund exposure reporting, a rollback aimed at cutting compliance burden for private fund managers.

headline: Agency management software leader Applied Systems taps insider Graham Blackwell as next CEO
summary: Applied Systems named longtime president Graham Blackwell as its incoming chief executive, succeeding Taylor Rhodes later in 2026, continuing a planned leadership transition at the insurance agency software provider.

headline: UnitedHealth's profit tops $6 billion in Q1 as medical costs ease and guidance rises
summary: UnitedHealth Group posted Q1 2026 earnings per share of $7.23 on revenue of $111.7 billion, beating estimates, and raised its full-year 2026 profit guidance as medical cost trends moderated.

headline: EU opens EUR9m fund for large-scale clinical AI imaging pilots
summary: The European Commission's Digital Europe Programme opened a call for proposals worth EUR9 million to fund large-scale pilots of cloud-based AI systems for medical imaging, focused on early detection of cancer and cardiovascular disease in hospitals.

headline: UK broker premiums post their steepest quarterly drop on record
summary: The Acturis Commercial Broking Index fell 3.6% year-on-year in Q1 2026, its largest decline since the index began in 2010, with fleet and combined liability lines driving the softening and squeezing broker commissions.

headline: Global insurance TPA market revenue grows by $32 billion year-over-year
summary: A new market report finds the insurance third-party administrator sector's global revenue expanded by roughly $32 billion year-over-year, with AI-driven claims automation cited as a key growth driver through 2030.

headline: Global insurance TPA market grows past $400 billion as AI claims automation spreads
summary: A 2026 market report finds insurance third-party administrator revenue grew roughly $32 billion year over year to reach about $404 billion, with AI-driven claims automation cited as a key growth driver through 2030.

headline: China's life insurers post steady premium growth as aging population drives demand
summary: Chinese life insurers reported premium income growth of about 7.3% year-over-year in the first quarter of 2026, with officials attributing the gains to accelerating retirement and protection-product demand from an aging population.

headline: Protective Life pushes beyond L&A, buys specialty P&C carrier Obsidian from Genstar
summary: Protective Life Insurance Company agreed to acquire specialty property & casualty platform Obsidian Insurance Holdings from private-equity owner Genstar Capital, a diversification move expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027.

headline: UK regulator's funded reinsurance crackdown could reshape bulk annuity deals
summary: The Bank of England's Prudential Regulation Authority is pushing ahead with Consultation Paper CP8/26, which would roughly double or more the capital insurers must hold against funded reinsurance used heavily in pension risk transfer deals; the consultation window closes July 31, 2026.

headline: CorVel embeds AI intelligence layer directly into its claims platform
summary: Workers' comp TPA CorVel launched "CorVel Connected," an AI layer inside its CareMC claims system offering automated claim summaries, generative-AI document review, intelligent assignment and reserve predictions to speed adjuster decisions.

headline: Benefits administrator TASC pours over $21 million into growth as plan complexity rises
summary: TASC, describing itself as the largest privately held benefits TPA in the US, said it is investing more than $21 million in sales expansion, its digital platform and ICHRA capabilities to help brokers and employers manage increasingly complex benefits plans.

headline: Gallagher Re promotes Russell Hails to lead its APAC managing general agent push
summary: The veteran broker's expanded role puts him in charge of building out Gallagher Re's MGA proposition across the Pacific, one of reinsurance's fastest-growing distribution channels.

headline: Alight brings back a former strategy chief to run its employer benefits unit
summary: Benefits administrator Alight named Dinesh Tulsiani, a former chief strategy officer who had rejoined the company as an adviser, President of Employer Solutions, while Susan Davies steps in as interim CFO.

headline: Long NHS waits push more Britons toward private medical insurance
summary: Persistent NHS waiting lists are driving increased UK consumer interest in private medical insurance, with buyers citing faster access to diagnostics and specialists as the main draw.

headline: Large 401(k) plans increasingly adopt automatic account portability
summary: Adoption of auto-portability, which automatically moves small balances into a new employer's plan when workers change jobs, is accelerating among large 401(k) plans in 2026, with adopting plans now covering more than 6.6 million active participants.

headline: LIMRA: U.S. individual life insurance sales extend strong growth into Q1 2026
summary: LIMRA's first-quarter 2026 data show individual life insurance sales continuing to build on 2025's record pace, with indexed universal life remaining the fastest-growing segment.

headline: Indexed universal life premium rises 14% in Q1 2026, extending a multi-year record run
summary: IUL new annualized premium reached $1.1 billion in the first quarter, up 14% year over year, with six of the ten largest carriers posting double-digit growth as insurers widen distribution.

headline: Sutter Health and Allina Health sign definitive agreement to form $26 billion nonprofit system
summary: The two nonprofit health systems moved closer to combining operations across California, Minnesota and Wisconsin, with Allina becoming Sutter's Upper Midwest Division and the deal expected to close by year-end pending regulatory approval.

headline: EU AI Act Now Classifies Insurance Underwriting as High-Risk, Forcing New Compliance Burden
summary: As of May 2026, the EU AI Act formally treats automated insurance underwriting as a high-risk AI use case, requiring insurers and insurtechs to maintain detailed documentation and conduct bias testing on their algorithms.

headline: US pension buyout volume cools sharply after blockbuster 2025 finish
summary: LIMRA data show US pension risk transfer sales fell 47% year-over-year to roughly $3.8 billion in Q1 2026, with single-premium buyout sales down 57%, a pullback attributed to deal timing that front-loaded activity into late 2025.

headline: TWFG expands agency footprint with Iowa-based Fortress Insurance Services deal
summary: TWFG completed its acquisition of Fortress Insurance Services, an independent Iowa agency, effective May 1, 2026, continuing a string of tuck-in agency and MGA purchases this year.

headline: Sutter Health and Allina Health agree to form $26 billion nonprofit system
summary: Sutter Health and Allina Health signed a definitive agreement to combine into a $26 billion nonprofit system spanning California, Minnesota and western Wisconsin, with Sutter committing $2 billion toward Allina's region.

headline: India opens insurance sector to 100% foreign direct investment under automatic route
summary: India's finance ministry amended foreign-exchange rules to permit 100% FDI in Indian insurance companies under the automatic route, extending the higher cap to brokers, reinsurance brokers, agents and other intermediaries while keeping state-run LIC capped at 20%.

headline: KKR leads $125 million raise for AI-driven claims administrator Reserv
summary: Claims technology firm Reserv, which serves roughly 200 insurers, captives, MGAs and brokers as an AI-native third-party administrator, closed a $125 million Series C led by KKR to expand its claims-processing capacity roughly sixtyfold over four years.

headline: Sedgwick debuts Omni, an integrated AI-powered claims and risk platform
summary: Sedgwick unveiled Omni, a proprietary digital ecosystem combining its claims data with AI and machine learning to support document summarization, triage, severity modeling, automated reserving and fraud detection across the claims lifecycle.

headline: Reinsurance rates keep softening through April renewals despite Middle East war-risk spike
summary: Property catastrophe reinsurance pricing continued to decline at April renewals on ample capacity and lower catastrophe losses, even as war-risk premiums for Middle East shipping routes jumped following regional tensions.

headline: UPMC to absorb four Ohio hospitals as CommonSpirit exits the Trinity Health System
summary: UPMC signed a definitive agreement to take over Trinity Health System's four Ohio Valley hospitals and clinics from CommonSpirit Health, marking UPMC's first entry into Ohio, with the deal expected to close this fall.

headline: UPMC signs definitive agreement to acquire CommonSpirit's Trinity Health System in Ohio
summary: UPMC will take over Trinity Health System's hospitals and clinics in the Ohio Valley, marking UPMC's first entry into Ohio, with the deal expected to close in fall 2026 pending regulatory approval.

headline: Corgi rolls out liability coverage for businesses deploying their own AI systems
summary: Insurtech-fintech Corgi launched a new insurance product aimed at protecting companies from financial and legal fallout tied to the AI systems they build or deploy, targeting a fast-growing category of emerging tech risk.

headline: Treasury convenes emergency talks with state regulators over insurers' private-credit exposure
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met with NAIC leadership and state insurance commissioners to discuss the rapid growth of insurers' private-credit holdings and the shifting of life and annuity reserves into offshore reinsurance structures.

headline: Insurer sues claims administrator over $2.48 million in unpaid claims
summary: Safety National and affiliated insurers sued third-party claims administrator S.A.F.E., alleging it walked away from contracts, left over 900 claims unhandled, and owes more than $5 million in claims-handling fees the insurer says were never earned.

headline: AI-focused startups swallow nearly all of Q1 insurtech funding
summary: Gallagher Re's Global InsurTech Report found AI-centered companies captured a record 95.2% of the $1.63 billion raised by insurtechs in Q1 2026, as investors concentrate capital on AI-driven underwriting, claims and investment tools.

headline: Roche to acquire digital pathology AI firm PathAI for up to $1.05 billion
summary: Roche agreed to acquire PathAI, whose AISight platform helps pathology labs move from manual slide review to AI-augmented digital workflows, in a deal worth up to $1.05 billion including milestone payments.

headline: TWFG continues agency and MGA acquisition streak with latest deal disclosure
summary: TWFG Insurance Services disclosed further agency and MGA acquisitions in an SEC filing, continuing its multi-year roll-up strategy of independent insurance distribution businesses.

headline: Ascensus scoops up AmericanTCS to bulk up trust and custody arm
summary: Recordkeeping giant Ascensus struck a deal to acquire AmericanTCS, adding trust, custody and technology-automation capabilities aimed at recordkeepers, bank trust companies, insurers and asset managers; terms weren't disclosed and the deal is slated to close in Q3 2026.

headline: Mayo Clinic's longtime CEO to depart at year's end
summary: Dr. Gianrico Farrugia announced he will step down as Mayo Clinic's president and CEO by the end of 2026 after leading the health system since 2019, with a successor expected to be named in November.

headline: Children's Hospital Los Angeles uses AI to match waitlisted patients to open appointments
summary: Children's Hospital Los Angeles is deploying AI across ambulatory clinics, its infusion center and operating room to match patients on waitlists with newly available appointment slots faster than manual scheduling allows.

headline: Australian MGA Hutch Underwriting Launches AI Tool That Quotes Broker Submissions in Minutes
summary: Hutch Underwriting launched an AI service called Dawn that reads broker submissions in any format, prices the risk, and automatically uploads a bindable quote into the broker's management system, starting with strata and professional-indemnity lines.

headline: US annuity sales cross $100 billion for a tenth straight quarter
summary: LIMRA reported total US annuity sales of roughly $107 billion in the first quarter of 2026, extending an unprecedented streak of quarterly sales above the $100 billion mark and reinforcing forecasts that full-year 2026 volume will stay above $450 billion.

headline: AI wholesale brokerage Novella lands $21M to build 'super producer' agents
summary: Novella, a New York-based AI-powered wholesale insurance broker co-founded by ex-Lemonade and Microsoft alumni, raised $21 million led by Brewer Lane Ventures with participation from insurer Arch, to open regional U.S. offices and expand its AI tooling for brokers.

headline: Outmarket AI raises $17 million to grow its insurance distribution platform
summary: The funding will let Outmarket AI expand its product aimed at helping agencies and brokers scale marketing and sales operations, part of a wave of AI-focused broker-tooling raises in 2026.

headline: MassMutual cashes in part of its Barings stake to a Japanese insurer
summary: MassMutual sold an 18% equity stake in asset manager Barings to Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance's parent MS&AD for about $1.44 billion, retaining 82% ownership and control while monetizing part of its embedded asset-management value.

headline: Insurers lean harder on AI for prior authorization as doctors cry foul over denials
summary: A growing bloc of payers has pledged to make at least 80% of prior-authorization decisions in real time by 2027 using AI, even as most physicians surveyed by the AMA say unchecked algorithmic review is driving up denial rates.

headline: Law firm maps shifting regulatory landscape for insurer private-credit investments
summary: A new legal overview details how state insurance regulators are adapting capital and disclosure rules as insurers keep expanding into private credit and other alternative assets within their general accounts.

headline: Insurers' private credit bets grow even as default rates climb
summary: Life insurers now represent roughly a quarter of private credit capital providers, with holdings up more than 20% in 2025 to about a tenth of total assets, but rising defaults in the asset class are drawing closer regulatory scrutiny of the exposure.

headline: Australian claims administrator rebuilds its entire operation on an AI claims platform
summary: Quartz Claims, a TPA operating across Australia and New Zealand, has moved its full claims operation onto Five Sigma's AI-powered claims management platform, including its Clive AI system, as core infrastructure. The move is part of a wider regional trend of TPAs replacing legacy claims systems with AI-native platforms.

headline: Japan raises iDeCo eligibility to age 70 and eases corporate DC matching rules
summary: Japan's pension reform, taking effect in April 2026, expands iDeCo eligibility to age 70, nearly triples the monthly contribution cap, and scraps the rule capping employee matching contributions at the employer's level in corporate DC plans.

headline: Fidelis and Howden go live on AI-driven Broker Connect submissions platform
summary: The Fidelis Partnership rolled out its AI-enabled Broker Connect platform with Howden as its first live broking partner, aiming to automate pre-bind submissions for complex commercial risks.

headline: Singapore Fintech Funding Jumped 78% in Early 2026 as Investors Chase Bigger Checks
summary: Fintech funding into Singapore-based companies rose 78% year-over-year in the first quarter of 2026 to roughly $160 million across 14 deals, with capital consolidating into fewer, larger rounds such as payments infrastructure firm Tazapay's $36 million extension.

headline: Zurich extends agentic AI underwriting platform toward more than 20 markets worldwide
summary: Zurich Insurance is scaling an AI risk-digitization platform built with insurtech Cytora to more than 20 countries over 16 months, after an initial five-country rollout cut manual submission triage time by roughly 80%, from 75 minutes to 15 minutes per case.

headline: Aon installs Pedro Penalva as new CEO of Latin America
summary: Aon named Pedro Penalva CEO of Latin America effective July 1, reporting directly to CEO Greg Case, as part of a broader regional leadership reshuffle spanning EMEA and Latin America.

headline: Cyclone-exposed Australian homeowners see dramatic premium relief
summary: Home insurance premiums in Australia's most cyclone-prone regions have fallen by as much as 37%, reflecting easing reinsurance costs and resilience investment after several years of steep hikes in high-risk coastal areas.

headline: Aon names Tracy-Lee Kus co-CEO of EMEA in regional leadership shake-up
summary: Aon appointed Tracy-Lee Kus, previously CEO of its Global Broking Center, as co-CEO for EMEA covering the UK, Ireland, South Africa and the Middle East, part of a wider restructuring of its regional leadership.

headline: Acrisure cuts 2,250 jobs as CEO points to AI reshaping the brokerage
summary: Broker giant Acrisure is eliminating about 11% of its global workforce in phases through 2027, with CEO Greg Williams telling staff that AI and digital platforms are changing how the business serves clients and creates value.

headline: EU widens AI Act's high-risk net to cover more insurance underwriting
summary: New draft guidance on the EU AI Act's Annex III, issued in May 2026, extended high-risk classification to more insurance underwriting use cases, including long-term care, personal pensions and public health cover, ahead of obligations for high-risk insurance AI systems taking effect in August 2026.

headline: AI investment-management platform Moment raises $78 million as adoption surges among large wealth firms
summary: Moment closed a $78 million Series C led by Index Ventures just months after its prior round, with its AI operating system now used by wealth firms collectively overseeing more than $10 trillion, up from about $300 billion roughly 18 months earlier.

headline: Insurer investment outsourcing tops $5.5 trillion as private markets expand
summary: Clearwater Analytics' 2026 Insurance Investment Outsourcing Report found third-party managed general account assets rose 23% year-over-year to $5.5 trillion, with insurers increasingly turning to outside managers for private-markets expertise.

headline: Sutter Health and Allina Health finalize plans for 39-hospital system
summary: The two nonprofit health systems reached a definitive agreement to combine, part of a broader rebound in hospital M&A that produced 18 announced deals in the second quarter of 2026, more than double the total from a year earlier.

headline: BriteCore rolls out eight embedded AI copilots for agency and carrier workflows
summary: BriteCore introduced a suite of eight AI copilots plus a new governance layer built on the Model Context Protocol, letting insurers and agencies plug both in-house and third-party AI agents directly into everyday policy and servicing workflows.

headline: Sutter Health and Allina Health sign definitive agreement for $26B nonprofit merger
summary: The combination would create a 39-hospital system spanning California, Wisconsin and Minnesota serving more than five million patients, with Sutter pledging a $2 billion investment in Allina's Upper Midwest markets.

headline: Survey finds only a third of UK consumers comfortable with AI-set insurance pricing
summary: A Guidewire consumer survey found roughly 30% of UK respondents would accept AI determining their policy pricing, with most wanting human oversight, transparency and independent regulation before trusting automated decisions more broadly.

headline: TPA Marpai projects positive cash flow after adding 192,000 new member lives
summary: Marpai said new client wins across its third-party administration and MarpaiRx pharmacy benefit management platforms are expected to add roughly 192,000 member lives, with the company projecting positive cash flow and EBITDA starting in August 2026.

headline: Marpai targets positive cash flow this month after adding 192,000 TPA and PBM member lives
summary: Health-tech TPA and PBM operator Marpai said it expects to turn cash-flow and EBITDA positive beginning August 2026 after securing commitments for roughly 192,000 new member lives rolling out through January 2027.

headline: Marpai projects positive cash flow starting August as TPA and PBM member base surges
summary: Marpai said an estimated 192,000 new member lives are rolling onto its TPA and MarpaiRx PBM platforms between August 2026 and January 2027 -- nearly a six-fold increase -- positioning the company to reach positive cash flow and EBITDA beginning this month.

headline: Flood-forecasting insurtech Previsico taps new CEO to push into the US
summary: The Loughborough University spinout named Mark Trumper, formerly of Axco Insurance Information, as chief executive to lead its next phase of international expansion.

headline: Insurance AI-agent startup Pace raises $46 million to scale back-office automation
summary: Pace, whose AI agents automate insurer back-office tasks like submission intake, policy servicing and claims handling, raised a $46 million Series B co-led by Thrive Capital and Sequoia Capital, after completing more than a quarter-million automated workflows for carriers including Prudential and WTW.

headline: India's Insurance Regulator Ties Top Executives' Pay Directly to Claims Service Quality
summary: IRDAI issued new norms requiring insurers to link half of senior executives' performance evaluation to customer-facing metrics such as claim settlement speed, grievance redressal and elimination of deceptive sales practices, with disclosure of claim closure and repudiation rates starting FY2026-27.

headline: AI-focused advisor startups drive an 83% jump in US wealthtech funding
summary: US wealthtech investment nearly doubled year over year in the first quarter of 2026, headlined by Jump, an AI platform for financial advisors, closing one of the period's largest rounds at $80 million.

headline: Global Insurance Premium Growth Cools to 1.3% for 2026 Amid Market Fragmentation
summary: New industry analysis shows worldwide insurance premium growth decelerating sharply in 2026 as economic fragmentation and softer pricing weigh on both life and non-life segments, even as the total premium pool keeps expanding.

headline: Commentary questions whether AI will sideline traditional TPAs entirely
summary: An industry op-ed argues that while AI is projected to automate the bulk of routine claims handling, TPAs are more likely to shift toward complex-case oversight and care coordination than disappear outright.

headline: AIG formally hands CEO reins to Eric Andersen as Zaffino moves to board chair
summary: AIG completed its planned leadership succession, with Eric Andersen becoming chief executive and joining the board while outgoing CEO Peter Zaffino shifts into the role of executive chairman.

headline: Mitigata secures $15 million to expand India cyber insurance underwriting
summary: India-focused insurtech Mitigata raised $15 million to build out cyber insurance coverage and risk-assessment tools for Indian businesses, part of a broader wave of AI-labeled underwriting funding.

headline: Corgi Insurance launches AI-native third-party administrator Corgi Claims
summary: Corgi Insurance launched Corgi Claims, a full-service TPA pairing a nationwide network of more than 5,000 licensed adjusters with AI that reviews every claim on report, scoring severity and flagging coverage issues and missing documents.

headline: CMS issues national playbook for new Medicaid work requirements
summary: CMS released nationwide implementation guidance for its Medicaid work-requirement rule, with states such as Arkansas and Montana beginning rollout in July 2026 ahead of a federal deadline; the agency projects about 2.3 million people will lose coverage.

headline: Private equity now owns more than 30% of US managing general agents
summary: Private equity firms are increasingly targeting MGAs as a growth platform because the fee-based, asset-light model scales without heavy capital requirements, with PE ownership now exceeding three in ten MGA entities in the US.

headline: Bed-blocking is costing the NHS an estimated 2.7 billion pounds a year
summary: Analysis finds delayed hospital discharges — with around 13,000 patients medically fit to leave remaining in NHS beds daily — are costing the health service roughly £2.7 billion annually, driven largely by social-care capacity shortfalls.

headline: Narayana Health to open India's first nurse-led 'smart' hospital in Bengaluru
summary: Narayana Health is building a new paperless, technology-enabled hospital in Bengaluru's Banashankari area that will be operationally run by nurses, part of an effort to groom nursing staff for future hospital leadership roles.

headline: Asia-Pacific insurtech market on track for nearly five-fold growth by 2035
summary: Industry forecasts put the Asia-Pacific insurtech market at roughly $28 billion in 2026, projected to grow about 19% annually to over $138 billion by 2035, powered by digital-first adoption across China, India, Japan and South Korea.

headline: Life insurers push AI deeper into underwriting decisions
summary: Carriers are increasingly automating life underwriting tasks, with reporting suggesting straight-through processing rates have jumped sharply and standard policy decisions can now be reached in minutes rather than days, though most gains so far come from speed rather than improved risk selection.

headline: Brussels issues draft guidance on which insurance AI systems count as high-risk
summary: The European Commission released draft, non-binding guidelines clarifying when AI systems used in insurance underwriting and pricing fall under the EU AI Act's high-risk regime, ahead of an August 2026 compliance deadline for such systems.

headline: Squeezed on fees, retirement recordkeepers lean harder on AI and pooled plans for growth
summary: A 2026 industry survey found pooled employer plan adoption jumped nearly 45% year over year, with recordkeepers turning to artificial intelligence to cut costs even as some expect it to shrink their own headcount within a few years.

headline: Ascensus launches national nonprofit 403(b) pooled employer plan
summary: Ascensus rolled out a new 403(b) Pooled Employer Plan for nonprofit organizations, with Newport serving as pooled plan provider and administrative fiduciary and Aprio providing independent investment oversight.

headline: Target-date funds with guaranteed income features surge past $103 billion
summary: Assets in target-date products carrying guaranteed income options grew 25% to $103 billion by mid-2025, with BlackRock's LifePath Paycheck series nearly tripling to $24 billion and TIAA's RetirePlus reaching $60 billion.

headline: Samaritan Health Services to join MultiCare Health System in 18-hospital affiliation
summary: The boards of both nonprofits approved an affiliation expected to close in fall 2026, with MultiCare committing $700 million over ten years to modernize Samaritan's Oregon facilities and expand its Medicaid and Medicare health plans.

headline: Vertafore rolls out new AI agents to automate carrier statement reconciliation for agencies
summary: Vertafore released two new Velocity AI agents inside its AgencyOne platform that automate carrier statement reconciliation and turn Outlook email activity into structured workflows, aiming to cut manual work for independent insurance agencies.

headline: Fulcrum taps veteran brokerage operations executive to drive AI workflow push
summary: Broker-facing AI automation platform Fulcrum brought on a brokerage operations veteran to lead its push into deeper AI workflow adoption, following the company's recent $25 million funding round.

headline: Workflow-automation startup Pace raises $46M to help insurance agencies cut manual work
summary: Pace closed a $46 million funding round aimed at automating back-office and servicing workflows for insurance agencies and brokerages, part of a wave of venture capital targeting broker productivity tools.

headline: ANV buys workers' comp MGA Specialty Comp from Hub's SPG unit
summary: Global intermediary platform ANV Group Holdings acquired Texas-based Specialty Comp Insurance Solutions, a monoline workers' compensation MGA that wrote about $250M in premium in 2025, from Hub International's Specialty Program Group.

headline: Federal auto-enrollment rules for new retirement plans expected imminently
summary: Treasury and IRS rulemaking on SECURE 2.0's mandatory auto-enrollment requirements for new 401(k) and 403(b) plans is expected soon, guidance plan sponsors have awaited since the mandate took effect.

headline: Global regulators publish AI governance question bank for insurers
summary: The International Association of Insurance Supervisors released a member-only supervisory question bank on AI governance and risk management, reflecting regulators' growing focus worldwide on responsible AI deployment across insurance and fintech.

headline: Epic pushes into the AI documentation market, challenging scribe startups
summary: Epic's new AI Charting tool listens in on patient visits, drafts clinical notes and suggests orders, leveraging the EHR giant's roughly 42% share of the acute-care hospital market to compete directly with well-funded ambient-scribe startups like Abridge and Ambience.

headline: Modern Wealth notches 22nd deal with $1.1B Florida RIA acquisition
summary: Modern Wealth Management agreed to acquire Clearwater-based Flaharty Asset Management, adding roughly $1.1 billion in client assets and an 18-person team as it pushes total AUM past $14 billion.

headline: HCA Healthcare snaps up 17 urgent care clinics to expand Southeast footprint
summary: HCA Healthcare acquired 17 urgent care clinics from Urgent Care Group across Charleston, Columbia, Myrtle Beach and Wilmington, rebranding them under its CareNow banner and pushing its urgent-care network past 390 locations.

headline: Convex Launches Tech-Enabled MGA Kinetic Insurance Services
summary: Specialty insurer Convex Group unveiled Kinetic Insurance Services, a new wholly owned, technology-enabled MGA targeting specialty and niche lines that will begin trading in the fourth quarter of 2026, backed by Convex and third-party capacity.

headline: SEC-registered advisers now manage $176.8 trillion, up 22% in a year
summary: The Investment Adviser Association's 2026 industry snapshot shows SEC-registered investment advisers managing a record $176.8 trillion in assets for 73.7 million clients, with the number of registered firms hitting a new high of 16,544.

headline: Pro Global opens a dedicated platform to help UK brokers expand across continental Europe
summary: Pro Global launched Pro Broker Europe GmbH, a new platform for UK-based brokers entering European markets, which has secured Lloyd's Europe accreditation to support cross-border market access.

headline: Ascension closes $3.9B AmSurg surgery-center deal after FTC-ordered divestitures
summary: Ascension completed its acquisition of ambulatory surgery operator AmSurg after agreeing to divest seven surgery centers to resolve FTC antitrust concerns, growing its ASC network to 300 centers across 35 states.

headline: PayPay completes purchase of majority stake in T&D Financial Life Insurance
summary: Japanese fintech PayPay finalized its acquisition of a 70.2% stake in T&D Financial Life Insurance Company from T&D Holdings, marking a notable fintech entry into life insurance underwriting.

headline: Honeycomb Insurance raises $40M to expand AI-powered real estate underwriting
summary: The digital insurer, which prices apartment and condo buildings without physical inspections using geospatial and aerial data, raised a round led by Zeev Ventures that brings its total funding to $95 million.

headline: MDIndia TPA Opens Fifth Chennai Claims Hub as South India Volumes Grow
summary: MDIndia Health Insurance TPA has launched a new claims-processing center of excellence in Chennai, growing local headcount past 450 staff and adding over 120 claims-review doctors as it deepens its 23-branch Tamil Nadu network.

headline: AI-native landlord insurer Honeycomb raises $40 million to expand no-inspection underwriting
summary: Honeycomb Insurance, which underwrites apartment buildings and condo associations using an AI-driven, no-inspection model, raised a $40 million round led by Zeev Ventures after exiting 2025 with $275 million in written premium.

headline: Managed-care stocks surge as Wall Street cheers cooler medical cost trends
summary: Shares of Humana, UnitedHealth and Cigna jumped after a wave of bullish analyst notes pointed to softening medical utilization and cost trends across the managed-care sector, with some analysts also flagging potential efficiency gains from AI adoption as a further tailwind.

headline: Convex Group launches Kinetic, a new technology-enabled specialty MGA
summary: Lloyd's-focused insurer Convex Group unveiled Kinetic Insurance Services, a wholly owned managing general agency built to trade specialty and niche lines using Convex's underwriting technology, with UK regulatory approval secured.

headline: SoftBank's PayPay to acquire 70% of T&D Financial Life in AI-driven insurance push
summary: PayPay agreed to acquire a 70.2% stake in T&D Financial Life for about JPY134.3 billion ($838 million) as part of a broader alliance with T&D Holdings to distribute insurance through its super-app and develop AI-powered products for Japan's aging population.

headline: Ascension closes $3.9 billion AmSurg deal after FTC-mandated divestitures
summary: Nonprofit health system Ascension closed its $3.9 billion acquisition of ambulatory surgery center operator AmSurg after agreeing to divest seven surgery centers to satisfy FTC competition concerns, becoming the country's third-largest ASC platform.

headline: Pro Global opens a dedicated platform to help UK brokers expand into Europe
summary: Pro Global launched Pro Broker Europe GmbH, a European broker-incubation platform aimed at UK-based brokers seeking to establish and scale operations on the continent, and secured Lloyd's Europe accreditation to back its regulatory credibility.

headline: WellSpan Health signs seven-year imaging and AI partnership with Philips
summary: WellSpan Health launched a seven-year alliance with Philips to advance diagnostic imaging, AI-enabled tools and broader clinical innovation across its health system.

headline: Empower elevates Daubenspeck to lead government and Taft-Hartley retirement units
summary: Empower named Marybeth Daubenspeck executive vice president overseeing its government and Taft-Hartley retirement plan businesses, putting her in charge of growth strategy, client relationships and operations for those segments.

headline: Most insurers plan to raise private-asset allocations over the next year, survey finds
summary: Goldman Sachs Asset Management's 2026 global insurance survey found 62% of insurers plan to increase private-asset allocations, with a net 38% planning to add asset-backed finance exposure within their general accounts.

headline: Industry submits final comments as DOL's alternative-assets 401(k) rule nears finish line
summary: Retirement-industry groups filed final comments on the Department of Labor's proposed rule clarifying fiduciary duties for selecting alternative investments in 401(k) plans, after the public comment period drew nearly 45,000 responses ahead of its June 1 close.

headline: Investment managers deploying AI in the front office jump sevenfold in a year
summary: A new survey found roughly seven in ten investment managers are now actively using artificial intelligence in front-office functions, up from about one in ten a year earlier, marking a sharp acceleration from pilot projects to production use.

headline: LIC Pushes RBI and SEBI for New Long-Duration Instruments as Annuity Liabilities Balloon
summary: Life Insurance Corporation of India's leadership said the insurer is engaging the central bank and market regulator to create longer-tenor investment instruments capable of matching annuity liabilities that stretch 30 to 50 years, as annuity demand from NPS retirees rises.

headline: Allianz eyes Portuguese insurer Caravela in deal that could nearly triple its local market share
summary: Allianz is reportedly in advanced talks to buy Caravela Seguros, Portugal's seventh-largest non-life insurer, a move that would lift Allianz's non-life market share in the country from roughly 1.3% to nearly 7% and push it past €1.15 billion in combined premiums.

headline: Pen Underwriting doubles UK SME cyber cover to £10 million as broker demand rises
summary: MGA Pen Underwriting raised its cyber cover limit to £10 million for risks incepting from July 1 and brought claims handling in-house, responding to broker demand from larger SME clients.

headline: GIFT City regulator formally licenses managing general agents for foreign insurers
summary: India's IFSCA has brought its Managing General Agents Regulations, 2026 into force, creating a formal registration and oversight framework for MGAs that underwrite or bind business on behalf of foreign insurers operating out of GIFT City.

headline: India's IFSC finance hub switches on a formal licensing regime for managing general agents
summary: The International Financial Services Centres Authority's new Managing General Agents Regulations, 2026, which set capital, governance, and binding-authority requirements for MGAs acting on behalf of foreign insurers in India's IFSCs, took effect in early June, giving global carriers a regulated route to delegate underwriting there.

headline: ANV Group acquires wholesale workers' comp specialist Associated Specialty Insurance Agency
summary: Global insurance intermediary platform ANV Group completed its acquisition of Associated Specialty Insurance Agency, a Pennsylvania-based wholesale commercial agency focused on workers' compensation coverage.

headline: Honeycomb Insurance raises $40 million to expand AI-powered property underwriting
summary: Digital insurer Honeycomb closed a $40 million round led by Zeev Ventures to expand its AI-driven underwriting platform for apartment buildings and condo associations, bringing total funding to $95 million after exiting 2025 with $275 million in written premium.

headline: ANV rounds out workers' comp platform with wholesale agency purchase
summary: ANV completed its acquisition of Associated Specialty Insurance Agency, a Pennsylvania wholesale agency with a 600-plus broker network focused on artisan contractor workers' comp risk, deepening ANV's specialty comp distribution alongside two other recent buys.

headline: Pacific Life Re strikes third block reinsurance deal in Japan
summary: Pacific Life Re completed its third asset-intensive block reinsurance transaction with Tokio Marine & Nichido Anshin Life, covering in-force whole life policies and aimed at reducing the Japanese insurer's long-term interest-rate risk.

headline: Philips survey: AI is already freeing clinicians 16+ workdays a year
summary: Philips' 2026 Future Health Index, drawing on over 2,000 clinicians and 20,000 patients across 10 countries, found nearly half of clinicians save upwards of 130 hours a year using AI tools and are seeing more patients as a result.

headline: Pacific Life Re strikes third asset-intensive reinsurance deal with Japan's Anshin Life
summary: Pacific Life Re completed its third block reinsurance transaction with Tokio Marine & Nichido Life's Anshin Life unit, covering in-force whole-of-life policies to help the Japanese insurer offload long-term interest rate risk.

headline: Satellite radar startup ICEYE raises over €1 billion, valuation tops €10 billion
summary: Finnish satellite-imaging company ICEYE raised more than €1 billion in a General Atlantic-led Series F round, pushing its valuation above €10 billion as it doubles annual satellite production for sovereign and insurance risk clients.

headline: Fidelity to bolt guaranteed lifetime income onto its target-date fund lineup
summary: Fidelity is launching Freedom Lifetime, a suite of target-date collective investment trusts that let plan sponsors offer employees the option to convert part of their target-date balance into a guaranteed income stream, available on Fidelity's recordkeeping platform in early 2027.

headline: Sutter Health and Allina Health sign definitive deal to form a $26 billion nonprofit system
summary: The combination would create a 39-hospital network spanning California and the Upper Midwest, with Allina retaining its brand as a regional division and Sutter committing over $2 billion in new investment for Minnesota and Wisconsin facilities.

headline: GEICO Completes Leadership Overhaul With New CFO Hire
summary: GEICO named David Foy, a former White Mountains Insurance Group finance chief, as its new CFO, rounding out the senior leadership team Berkshire Hathaway installed at the auto insurer under CEO Nancy Pierce.

headline: Alternative capital and ILS funds increasingly back US MGA growth
summary: A growing share of US managing general agents are turning to insurance-linked securities and other alternative capital rather than traditional reinsurers to fund underwriting capacity, according to Conning research highlighted by Gallagher Re.

headline: John Hancock rolls out an AI-enabled recordkeeping platform built on FIS technology
summary: John Hancock's new Future Choice platform runs on FIS Omni alongside other technology partners, intended to support a broader range of plan types, including pooled employer plans, while embedding AI and API-driven data capabilities.

headline: Fidelity to launch target-date funds with built-in guaranteed income, backed by Nationwide
summary: Fidelity announced Freedom Lifetime, a target-date collective investment trust suite adding a guaranteed lifetime income option for plan sponsors, with Nationwide serving as the insurance partner starting in early 2027.

headline: UK Government Pours £30 Million Into AI Cancer-Diagnosis Rollout
summary: The UK government announced nearly £30 million in funding to expand AI-assisted X-ray analysis to every NHS trust in England by 2029 and pilot new AI diagnostic tools at a dozen additional sites. Existing AI tools have already helped over four million patients get faster lung-cancer diagnoses.
source_name: GOV.UK / Department of Health and Social Care

headline: GEICO names David Foy chief financial officer, completing its leadership overhaul
summary: GEICO appointed insurance-industry veteran David Foy, formerly CFO of White Mountains Insurance Group and Hartford Life, as its new chief financial officer, filling the last major gap in the carrier's rebuilt executive team under CEO Nancy Pierce.

headline: Recordkeepers warn fee compression is becoming an existential threat at industry roundtable
summary: At the 8th Annual RPA Record Keeper Roundtable, industry leaders described a squeeze between shrinking fees and rising demands for AI, cybersecurity and expanded participant services, while eyeing financial wellness as a growth avenue.

headline: BlackRock winds down ESG-labeled target-date fund, thinning the sustainable-TDF field
summary: BlackRock said it will liquidate its LifePath ESG Index Retirement Fund in October, leaving only Fidelity and GuideStone as managers still offering a dedicated sustainable target-date fund.

headline: New Federal Rules Would Force TPAs to Disclose Compensation on Self-Funded Plans
summary: A Department of Labor proposal, converging with 2026 appropriations-law changes, would require pharmacy benefit managers and the third-party administrators contracting with them to give employer plan sponsors detailed upfront and semiannual compensation disclosures for plan years beginning July 1, 2026.

headline: Sixfold rolls out an AI agent that can quote and bind P&C policies end to end
summary: Insurtech Sixfold launched an AI underwriting agent aimed at giving property and casualty insurers straight-through processing from submission to bound policy, part of a broader industry push to automate underwriting workflows.

headline: Cigna's Express Scripts sues Tennessee to block law forcing PBMs to divest pharmacies
summary: Express Scripts and the PCMA trade group filed a federal lawsuit challenging Tennessee's FAIR Rx Act, which would bar pharmacy benefit managers from owning pharmacies, arguing the law is unconstitutional and would shutter a major Memphis specialty pharmacy. CVS Caremark had already filed a similar challenge weeks earlier.

headline: Envestnet adds AI explainability and advisor-decisioning tools at Elevate 2026
summary: Envestnet unveiled new AI explainability and workflow features for its wealth data platform at its Elevate 2026 conference, aiming to give advisors more transparency into automated recommendations.

headline: Federal regulators close out settlements with all three major drug middlemen
summary: Following settlements with Express Scripts and CVS Caremark earlier in 2026, the FTC reached a proposed settlement with Optum Rx over alleged anticompetitive insulin-pricing practices, completing a sweep of the three dominant PBMs alongside new federal transparency and rebate-reform laws taking effect through 2029.

headline: Group Benefit Services acquires Sacramento TPA Integrity Administrators
summary: Group Benefit Services acquired Integrity Administrators, a longstanding Sacramento-based third-party administrator, in a deal the companies say will expand service capacity for benefits clients.

headline: Centene offers buyouts to most of its 61,000-person workforce as margins tighten
summary: Centene confirmed it is offering a voluntary separation program across the bulk of its employee base as the Medicaid-focused insurer works to cut costs amid declining earnings.

headline: IRDAI orders health insurers and hospitals onto new claims-speed and billing scorecards
summary: India's insurance regulator introduced performance scorecards tracking claim settlement speed and billing accuracy for insurers and hospitals, alongside simpler standardized health policies meant to boost low insurance penetration.

headline: IAG's venture arm backs crisis-support app Sonder to extend care beyond claims
summary: Australia's IAG made a strategic minority investment in Sonder through its Firemark Ventures arm, aiming to extend the 24/7 mental-health and safety platform to customers during catastrophic weather events, not just its own workforce.

headline: Centene overhauls leadership and offers buyouts as ACA losses bite
summary: After shedding more than two million ACA exchange members, insurer Centene restructured its executive ranks and offered companywide voluntary buyouts in an effort to cut costs.

headline: Congress's PBM reform law starts delinking compensation from drug prices as FTC presses Express Scripts and Caremark
summary: The Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026 will base Medicare Part D PBM pay on flat service fees rather than rebates starting 2028 and bans Medicaid spread pricing, while the FTC's Express Scripts settlement is expected to cut patient drug costs by up to $7 billion over a decade.

headline: Three-quarters of US health systems now use or are piloting AI platforms, survey finds
summary: Half of respondents run three or more AI applications, and more than half of those able to measure ROI report at least a 2x return, with documentation, imaging triage and virtual nursing among the leading use cases.

headline: Study projects India's insurtech sector nearing $1 billion in fresh funding
summary: A joint industry report forecasts private investment into Indian insurtech topping $1 billion over the next year as the market shifts from agent-led sales toward platform-driven, data-based distribution.

headline: CMS proposes new electronic prior-authorization mandate for drug coverage
summary: A newly proposed CMS interoperability rule would require payers to support electronic prior authorization for drugs, shrink decision-turnaround times, and publish more transparency data, extending prior-auth reform into pharmacy benefits.

headline: Sutter Health moves to absorb Allina Health in $26 billion multi-state tie-up
summary: Sutter Health announced plans to acquire Minneapolis-based Allina Health, forming a combined nonprofit system spanning California, Minnesota and Wisconsin with 39 hospitals and roughly 88,000 employees, expected to close by year-end 2026.

headline: NOAA issues most favorable Atlantic hurricane forecast in over a decade
summary: NOAA's 2026 outlook puts a 55% chance on a below-normal Atlantic hurricane season, the first such forecast since 2015, though insurers say a single landfalling storm could still drive major losses and are holding firm on coastal deductibles.

headline: India's pension body to launch bundled pension-and-health NPS product
summary: PFRDA plans to roll out 'NPS Swasthya' within roughly two months, a scheme pairing a pension account with top-up health insurance coverage, with Aditya Birla Health Insurance signed on as the first participating insurer.

headline: Wealthtech leaders sketch out how AI will reshape advisor tools next
summary: Ten wealthtech executives and investors weighed in on where artificial intelligence is headed in wealth management, pointing to next-best-action recommendations, planning alerts and risk flags as the next wave of features advisors will adopt.

headline: US life/annuity industry income falls 18% as premiums drop $36 billion in Q1
summary: An early look at first-quarter 2026 results shows the U.S. life and annuity sector's total income declined 18% year-over-year as premiums and annuity considerations fell by roughly $36 billion industry-wide.

headline: US RIA industry assets swell past $176 trillion as consolidation concentrates at the top
summary: New industry data shows registered investment advisers now manage a record $176.8 trillion in assets, a 22.3% jump, with record numbers of advisers and clients served. The report notes that 77% of RIA assets now sit with just 7% of firms, as mega-RIAs continue to scale largely through market appreciation and acquisitions rather than organic growth.

headline: US health insurers push through steepest ACA marketplace premium hikes in years
summary: Insurers filed for roughly 21.7% average benchmark premium increases on 2026 ACA marketplace plans, the largest jump since 2018, driven by rising drug and medical costs including GLP-1 spending.

headline: Centene opens buyout window for most of its 61,000 employees
summary: Centene is offering voluntary separation packages to the bulk of its workforce after enrollment fell sharply, particularly in its ACA marketplace business, which dropped from 5.6 million to 3.6 million members, with layoffs possible if too few volunteer.

headline: Sixfold debuts an AI underwriting agent built with major carriers
summary: Having previously raised a $30 million Series B, Sixfold launched its AI Underwriter, an agent developed over three years with large insurers to speed up submission triage, risk assessment and pricing guidance.

headline: Singapore overhauls rulebook for single-family offices
summary: A revised regulatory framework for single-family offices from Singapore's central bank took effect in mid-June 2026, streamlining setup procedures for new offices while tightening ongoing monitoring, as the city-state's family-office count has grown past 1,500 from under 200 seven years ago.

headline: Singapore's AI scribe tool spreads across the country's public hospital clusters
