summary: Aon's 2026 Climate and Catastrophe Insight report finds severe convective storms have driven $50 billion in insured losses over two years, displacing hurricanes as the leading source of US insured weather losses, especially in suburban housing markets.

headline: Global MGA market on pace to more than double to $128.7 billion by 2034
summary: A market research report values the global managing general agent segment at $63.4 billion in 2025 and projects an 8.2% compound annual growth rate through 2034 as carriers keep delegating underwriting authority to MGAs.

headline: IAIS flags private credit and AI adoption as top global insurance supervisory priorities
summary: The International Association of Insurance Supervisors' mid-year Global Insurance Market Report highlighted growing life-insurer allocations to private credit, geoeconomic fragmentation and rapid AI adoption in underwriting as the leading risks supervisors are monitoring worldwide.

headline: Orion becomes one of the first wealthtech firms to earn ISO 42001 AI certification
summary: Orion passed an independent audit to earn ISO/IEC 42001 certification for the AI management system governing its Denali AI layer, becoming the first portfolio-accounting provider and second advisor-tech firm overall to reach the standard.

headline: Louisiana doubles insurer cancellation notice period to 60 days
summary: Under Act No. 182, Louisiana insurers must now give at least 60 days' written notice before canceling or non-renewing most home, auto and commercial property policies, up from 30 days previously, except in cases of nonpayment.

headline: More health systems drop out of Medicare Advantage networks as July 1 deadlines hit
summary: Brown University Health physicians went out of network with UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage plans and Moffitt Cancer Center dropped Humana MA plans effective July 1, continuing a wave of provider-payer contract breaks.

headline: UK insurers flag AI-fabricated case law as a fresh professional indemnity risk
summary: UK insurers and law firms issued guidance warning that lawyers and other professionals relying on generative AI that invents fake case citations now represents a genuine and growing professional indemnity exposure.

headline: Europe's largest pension manager installs permanent chief executive
summary: Dutch pension giant APG Asset Management formally appointed Alineke van den Berge-Blindenbach as chief executive effective July 1, 2026, confirming a role she had held on an interim basis since March after previously serving as chief operating officer.

headline: New DOL disclosure rule for TPAs and PBMs on self-funded ERISA plans takes effect
summary: A Department of Labor regulation proposed in January 2026 requiring third-party administrators and PBMs to give employers extensive advance fee and compensation disclosures when contracting on self-funded ERISA group health plans became applicable for plan years beginning on or after July 1, 2026.

headline: Cigna's leadership handoff becomes official as Evanko takes the CEO seat from Cordani
summary: Brian Evanko formally became Cigna's chief executive on July 1, succeeding David Cordani, who moves into the executive chair role after nearly three decades leading the insurer.

headline: Life insurers work to reassure a wearier clientele as 2026 progresses
summary: Coverage of 2026 life and annuity sales messaging finds carriers leaning on guarantees and income features to address client fatigue with market volatility and keep demand steady through the back half of the year.

headline: 401(k) elective deferral cap rises to $24500 for 2026
summary: The IRS increased the annual elective deferral limit for 401(k) and similar plans to $24,500 for 2026, requiring recordkeeping platforms and plan sponsors to update contribution systems and participant communications.

headline: Commercial P&C pricing keeps softening as insurer profitability improves
summary: Analysts expect commercial insurance conditions to keep favoring buyers in 2026 as stronger insurer profitability and increased competition slow premium growth, even as catastrophe exposure remains elevated.

headline: CMS reopens Medicare Advantage bidding after revising star-rating scores
summary: CMS is recalculating 2026 Medicare Advantage star ratings, restoring some bonus payments to plans and reopening the 2027 bid process as a result. The move comes as average MA-PD star ratings have declined and CMS's finalized CY2027 rules narrow the margin for plans to earn top quality scores.

headline: Collective investment trusts keep gaining ground in the target-date fund market
summary: Twenty years after the Pension Protection Act enabled automatic enrollment, collective investment trusts are increasingly displacing mutual funds in target-date lineups as plan sponsors seek lower, more customizable fee structures, with total target-date series reaching a record 164 by year-end 2025.

headline: UnitedHealthcare and Humana retreat from Medicare Advantage counties for 2026
summary: The two largest Medicare Advantage insurers are pulling back for 2026, with UnitedHealthcare exiting 225 counties while entering just 14, and Humana exiting 198 counties while entering five, as CMS's 2026 final rule also tightens prior-authorization and appeals protections.

headline: Nevada moves to let home insurers exclude wildfire losses from standard policies
summary: Nevada will permit homeowners insurers to carve wildfire coverage out of standard policies starting in 2026, part of a broader wave of state-level moves on wildfire exposure management following record catastrophe losses.

headline: 401(k) recordkeeper consolidation stalls on valuation gaps and shifting business models
summary: A wave of expected recordkeeper M&A has cooled in 2026, with advisors and dealmakers pointing to mismatched valuation expectations and recordkeepers' pivot toward broader financial-wellness services as reasons deals are taking longer to close.

headline: US commercial P&C premiums post first quarterly decline in nearly nine years
summary: Average commercial property-casualty premiums fell in the first quarter of 2026, ending a 33-quarter streak of increases, as ample capital and intensifying competition push property rates down even while casualty lines keep hardening.

headline: Cigna's Brian Evanko formally succeeds David Cordani as CEO
summary: The Cigna Group's planned leadership transition took effect, with Brian Evanko becoming CEO while David Cordani moved into the role of executive chair after leading the health insurer for more than a decade.

headline: Broker M&A hit a record 695 deals in 2025 as private equity kept buying
summary: Tracking firm OPTIS Partners counted 695 insurance agency and broker M&A transactions in 2025 worth $4.3 billion in disclosed value, up about 27% year-over-year, with private equity involved in 69% of disclosed deals.

headline: IRDAI Licenses Prudential-HCL Joint Venture as India's Eighth Standalone Health Insurer
summary: India's insurance regulator granted a certificate of registration to Prudential HCL Health Insurance, a 70:30 joint venture between UK-based Prudential and India's HCL Group, making it the country's eighth standalone health insurer.

headline: Global reinsurance capital hits record $790 billion as catastrophe bond issuance sets first-half record
summary: Guy Carpenter data show reinsurer capacity and abundant risk appetite pushed cat bond issuance to an all-time first-half high of $17.3 billion, while property catastrophe rates fell the most since the late 1990s at mid-year renewals.

headline: AIG names Nancy Bewlay global chief underwriting officer
summary: AIG appointed Nancy Bewlay, formerly AXA's group chief underwriting and pricing officer, as executive vice president and global chief underwriting officer effective September 8, 2026, reporting to CEO Eric Andersen.

headline: BCG says asset managers need a new growth playbook as fee pressure mounts
summary: Boston Consulting Group's 2026 global asset management report argues the industry must rethink its economics as traditional fee-based growth slows and firms turn to alternatives and AI for margin.

headline: AIG hires AXA veteran Nancy Bewlay as global chief underwriting officer
summary: AIG named Nancy Bewlay, most recently AXA's group chief underwriting and pricing officer, as its new executive vice president and global chief underwriting officer effective September 8, bringing more than 30 years of underwriting leadership experience from AXA, Swiss Re and C.V. Starr.

headline: PwC's midyear outlook sees insurance distribution M&A staying resilient despite AI uncertainty
summary: PwC's 2026 midyear insurance deals outlook finds that despite growing deal scrutiny tied to how AI may disrupt distribution, the underlying strategic and financial drivers behind broker and MGA M&A remain firmly intact.

headline: Trio of Focus Financial Network Firms Merge to Form $10 Billion RIA
summary: Coastal Bridge Advisors completed a three-way combination with Waddell & Associates and One Charles Private Wealth, creating a single advisory firm with more than $10 billion in assets across seven offices.

headline: Property Catastrophe Reinsurance Prices Drop Sharply at Mid-Year Renewals
summary: Brokers reported risk-adjusted price cuts of roughly 15-40% across U.S. property treaty and facultative placements at the July 1 renewal date, as abundant capital and strong reinsurer profits softened the market.

headline: Bspoke Group's Tim Smyth Named New Chairman of the MGAA
summary: The Managing General Agents' Association appointed Tim Smyth to succeed Charles Manchester as chairman following ten years in the role, effective around the trade body's annual conference.

headline: US ETF inflows smash records, topping $1 trillion at the year's halfway mark
summary: Second-quarter inflows into US-listed ETFs hit a record $560 billion, pushing first-half totals over $1 trillion and putting the industry on pace for roughly $2.3 trillion for the full year, per State Street's flow data.

headline: US age-adjusted death rate hits a record low as CDC releases fresh 2025 data
summary: Provisional CDC data published July 2 showed the nation's age-adjusted death rate fell 4.6% in 2025 to 689.2 per 100,000 people, the lowest rate ever recorded, a data point providers and payers are citing in mortality and underwriting trend discussions.
source_name: Alston & Bird (Health Care Week in Review)

headline: Alliant lures former Hub executive to lead expanded M&A advisory push
summary: Alliant Insurance Services named Justin Sorensen, formerly a Hub International practice leader, to the newly created role of executive vice president within Alliant's mergers and acquisitions advisory team, reporting to the president of Alliant P&C.

headline: Asia's largest insurtech gathering spotlights agentic AI and underinsurance
summary: ITC Asia 2026 drew more than 1,500 industry leaders to Singapore for sessions on turning agentic AI into measurable underwriting and claims ROI, alongside dedicated tracks on Japan's evolving insurance ecosystem and expanding coverage across India.

headline: AI-linked layoffs ripple through tech and finance sectors, insurance included
summary: A labor-market analysis found tech and finance employers, including insurance-adjacent firms, are shedding roughly 28,000 jobs a month as AI automation reshapes staffing needs across broker and carrier back offices.

headline: Wealth Enhancement scoops up second Shufro Rose team with $554 million in assets
summary: Wealth Enhancement agreed to acquire the Kaminsky-Silverman Group from New York-based Shufro Rose, its second deal with the firm in as many months, adding roughly $554 million in client assets.

headline: Elevance sues CMS seeking same Medicare Advantage star-rating fix given to Clover
summary: Elevance Health sued CMS and HHS, arguing it deserves the same star-ratings recalculation a court forced for Clover Health, a change Elevance says would be worth about $115 million in quality bonus payments.

headline: UK underwriting body warns dealmakers are leaning too hard on cyber cover
summary: The International Underwriting Association cautioned that warranty-and-indemnity insurers may be over-relying on cyber insurance to cover M&A transaction risk, flagging coverage gaps underwriters need to address.

headline: Specialist Risk Group snaps up London MGA and wholesale broker Superian
summary: SRG acquired Superian Insurance Group, a London wholesaler, retailer and MGA known for medical malpractice and healthcare liability expertise, expanding SRG's specialist distribution capacity.

headline: ANNA Money embeds Admiral Business insurance directly into its small-business app
summary: Business account and tax platform ANNA Money partnered with Admiral Business to let small-business customers browse cover options, get information and obtain insurance quotes without leaving the ANNA app.

headline: Hagerty to buy UK motorcycle broker Bennetts in £34 million deal
summary: Classic-car insurer Hagerty agreed to acquire Bennetts, the UK's second-largest specialty motorcycle insurance broker, from Lucida Group for about £34 million, aiming to build a combined enthusiast platform across bikes and cars.

headline: Allianz spins up a digital-only car insurance brand built for speed
summary: Allianz UK introduced Slick Cover, a digital-first motor insurance brand run as a managing general agent, which went from concept to issuing its first policy in under six months as part of Allianz's push for faster digital product launches.

headline: CMS proposes 2027 hospital payment rule pushing more care into outpatient settings
summary: CMS released its CY2027 Hospital Outpatient and Ambulatory Surgical Center proposed rule, expanding site-neutral payment policy and other measures meant to curb Medicare spending and steer procedures toward lower-cost sites of care.

headline: Singapore to merge three separate hospital apps into one national health app
summary: Singapore's public healthcare clusters announced they will unify the NHG, NUHS and SingHealth patient apps into a single enhanced HealthHub app launching in November 2026, aiming to cut digital fragmentation for patients.

headline: Boutique manager Centenary bets on AI and machine learning to reinvent investment management
summary: Centenary Asset Management is embedding AI and machine-learning tools across research and portfolio construction, reflecting a broader industry push toward algorithm-assisted decision-making in asset and wealth management.

headline: General Atlantic in advanced talks for $1.82 billion Nuvama Wealth stake
summary: Private equity firm General Atlantic is negotiating to buy PAG's roughly 54% holding in Nuvama Wealth Management, though a rally in Nuvama's share price has widened the valuation gap between buyer and seller.

headline: Standard Insurance exits individual annuity sales, shifts book to Pacific Guardian Life
summary: The Standard signed a definitive agreement to transition its individual annuities business to Pacific Guardian Life so it can concentrate on workplace benefits, with the deal expected to close in early 2027 pending regulatory approval.

headline: Fiduciary Services Group acquires Florida TPA Pension Investors Corporation
summary: The parent of DWC – The 401(k) Experts bought the 40-year-old Florida third-party administrator, adding roughly 900 retirement plans and deepening FSG's presence across the Southeast.

headline: Australian Pension Funds Post Single-Digit Returns for the Latest Financial Year
summary: Australia's A$4.5 trillion superannuation industry is reporting fiscal-year results with major funds like Australian Retirement Trust expecting default high-growth returns of about 9%, below the prior year's pace as markets cooled.

headline: EPFO rolls out EPS 2026, requires pension claims to be settled within 20 days
summary: India's retirement fund body formally replaced its 1995-era pension scheme with EPS 2026 from July 1, keeping the minimum pension at ₹1,000 while mandating faster claims processing and interest penalties on unjustified delays.

headline: UnitedHealth's Optum wraps up purchase of benefits-account platform Alegeus
summary: Optum Financial finalized its takeover of Alegeus Technologies, a provider of HSA/FSA/HRA and COBRA administration software, aiming to broaden the range of consumer health-payment tools it can offer employers and health plans.

headline: CMS's proposed 2027 outpatient rule would deepen 340B payment cuts
summary: CMS's newly proposed CY2027 hospital outpatient payment rule would raise base rates 2.4% while further cutting reimbursement for drugs bought under the 340B discount program and tightening breakthrough-device payment pathways.

headline: SEC-registered advisors now oversee $176.8 trillion, up 22% year-over-year
summary: More than 16,544 SEC-registered investment advisers collectively manage $176.8 trillion in assets as of mid-July, up 22.3% from a year earlier, with AI emerging as the dominant theme in new wealthtech product announcements.

headline: Treasury Confirms BlackRock, Vanguard and State Street ETFs for New Child Savings Accounts
summary: The US Treasury said the newly launched tax-advantaged "Trump Accounts" for children will offer index ETFs from BlackRock, Vanguard and State Street, with a government seed contribution for babies born between 2025 and 2028 and several employers matching it.

headline: AI-driven auto MGA Mile Auto scoops up Georgia agency to bulk up Southeast distribution
summary: Pay-per-mile insurance MGA Mile Auto acquired The Insurance House, combining its AI and computer-vision underwriting tech with the Georgia agency's six-decade network of independent agents to form a nearly $100 million premium platform.

headline: India's insurance regulator licenses Prudential-HCL joint venture as newest standalone health insurer
summary: IRDAI granted a certificate of registration to Prudential HCL Health Insurance, a 70:30 joint venture between UK-based Prudential and India's HCL Group, making it the eighth standalone health insurer in the country and the third new insurance license the regulator has issued so far in 2026.

headline: OU Health hands the CEO role to its COO as founding chief executive retires
summary: Jonathan Curtright, who had served as chief operating officer, became president and CEO of OU Health on July 1, succeeding founding CEO Richard Lofgren; under Curtright's operational leadership the Oklahoma system's annual revenue nearly doubled to a projected $3.7 billion with double-digit growth in admissions.

headline: Malibu Life USA completes acquisition of TruSpire, launching its U.S. retail annuity business
summary: Malibu Life Holdings closed its purchase of TruSpire Retirement Insurance Company, rebranding it as Malibu Life USA and establishing the unit as the company's origination engine for U.S. retail fixed indexed annuities.

headline: Foreign Investors Rush Into India's Insurance Sector After FDI Cap Removal
summary: With India's insurance FDI limit raised to 100%, IRDAI has already cleared one foreign investor's bid to raise its stake in a domestic venture and is reviewing another, signaling accelerating foreign entry into the market.

headline: IRDAI Plans to Overhaul Agent Commission Structure to Curb Mis-Selling
summary: India's insurance regulator is preparing a consultation paper that would spread distributor commissions over a policy's full life instead of paying them upfront, aiming to reduce mis-selling driven by front-loaded incentives.

headline: WealthTech leads another active week of fintech fundraising
summary: Wealthtech startups accounted for five of the 17 fintech funding deals tracked in the first days of July, continuing a strong run for advisor- and RIA-focused technology investment following a record Q1 for the category.

headline: JPMorgan sees no floor yet for falling reinsurance prices after steep midyear drop
summary: JPMorgan analysts say property catastrophe reinsurance rates fell roughly 16% at the July 1 renewal, an acceleration from January, as record capital and low catastrophe losses continue shifting pricing power toward cedents with little sign of stabilizing.

headline: Willis Re adds veteran marine broker to reinsurance team
summary: Willis Re hired David Kim, a 20-year marine and non-marine reinsurance veteran and former Korean Re London chief executive, as a reinsurance broker to bolster its marine practice.

headline: MGAA installs Bspoke Group's Tim Smyth as new chairman
summary: The UK's Managing General Agents' Association named Tim Smyth, chair of Bspoke Group, as its new chairman, succeeding Charles Manchester after his decade-long tenure leading the trade body.

headline: White Glove Insurance spins up brokerage tech subsidiary
summary: White Glove Insurance launched White Glove Technology, a new subsidiary building a full-service platform meant to consolidate the fragmented vendor stack independent brokerages rely on, with a phased rollout planned through Q4 2026.

headline: New Indian institute launches insurtech leadership training program at GIFT City
summary: NeoProEd kicked off the first cohort of its Insurtech Professional Program in partnership with GIFT International FinTech Institute, a 10-week practitioner-led course capped by a residential capstone in Gandhinagar aimed at building India's next generation of insurance and insurtech leaders.

headline: MGA premiums surge to $108.7 billion in 2025 as capacity providers grow choosier
summary: AM Best's annual MGA segment report found delegated-authority premium jumped nearly 18% in 2025, marking a fifth straight year of double-digit growth, though analysts flagged tighter carrier scrutiny of capacity deployment ahead.

headline: Softening P&C market fuels fresh megadeal speculation, with Zurich-Beazley as bellwether
summary: Dealmakers point to Zurich's $10.9 billion all-cash agreement to acquire Lloyd's insurer Beazley as a sign more billion-dollar-plus insurance acquisitions could surface in the second half of 2026 as underwriting conditions soften.

headline: ACA marketplace enrollment drops by millions as subsidy fight continues
summary: With enhanced ACA premium subsidies expired, marketplace enrollment has fallen by millions, and the Trump administration and policy analysts continue to disagree over how much of the drop reflects affordability versus fraud crackdowns.

headline: India's insurance regulator floats spreading agent commissions across a policy's full life
summary: IRDAI is considering replacing large upfront commissions with payouts spread over the life of a policy to curb mis-selling, with a distribution consultation paper expected by end of July according to chairman Ajay Seth.

headline: Wealthtech roundup: AI-native platforms and prospecting tools gain traction among large RIAs
summary: A weekly wealthtech roundup covers AI-native wealth manager Arca raising $64 million with backing from Vanguard's former CEO, and a $17 billion RIA naming a money-in-motion prospecting platform as its enterprise-wide tool.

headline: Singapore regulator lays out guardrails for autonomous AI agents in finance
summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore, working with banks and fintechs, published a framework called SAFR that would require AI agents handling payments, treasury and advisory tasks to operate within pre-approved boundaries with real-time validation and audit trails rather than unchecked autonomy.

headline: Schroders sheds UK advice arm to Söderberg & Partners as Nuveen takeover advances
summary: Schroders agreed to sell Benchmark, its UK-based integrated financial-advice business, to Söderberg & Partners, streamlining its wealth arm just before Nuveen's pending roughly $13.5 billion acquisition of the asset manager closes.

headline: UK bulk annuity market reshaped as new insurer owners complete pension deals
summary: XPS Group's latest trustee briefing notes that Athora's acquisition of Pension Insurance Corporation and Brookfield's purchase of Just Group have both received regulatory approval and closed, adding fresh competition to the UK bulk annuity market as insurers push toward a forecast £40-55 billion of pension risk transfer volume in 2026.

headline: Insurers described as facing an 'agility crisis' as risk outpaces response speed
summary: An industry analysis argues insurers face a widening gap between how quickly climate, cyber and economic risks are changing and how quickly carriers can adjust pricing and products in response.

headline: Agentic AI Platform mea Reports Broker Productivity Gains Across 20-Country Rollout
summary: Insurance operations platform mea says insurers, brokers and MGAs using its agentic AI tools for underwriting, claims and broking are seeing roughly 30% higher broker productivity and 40% more underwriting capacity across more than 30 live deployments processing over $400 billion in premium.

headline: EBSA's 2026 agenda lists roughly 20 pending retirement-plan rulemakings
summary: The Labor Department's Employee Benefits Security Administration released its 2026 regulatory agenda on July 3, outlining guidance projects at various stages including an investment-selection safe harbor, an ESG-replacement rule, and several SECURE 2.0 implementation items.

headline: Number of Licensed Insurance Brokers in India Climbs 40% Over Five Years
summary: India had 751 licensed insurance brokers as of early July 2026, a 40% increase over five years, reflecting both greater insurance complexity and rising demand from buyers for professional broking guidance.

headline: NeoProEd launches to close India's insurtech talent gap
summary: NeoProEd, founded by veteran insurance leaders, launched its Insurtech Professional Program with the GIFT International FinTech Institute to train talent for India's fast-growing, AI- and embedded-insurance-driven sector.

headline: QBE buys out its Indian joint-venture partner to take full control of local insurer
summary: Australia's QBE Insurance Group completed the purchase of the remaining 51% stake in Raheja QBE General Insurance from building-materials firm Prism Johnson for about $34 million, giving QBE full ownership after IRDAI approval and setting up a rebrand of the unit.

headline: Catastrophe-property MGU pulls in $460 million-plus as admitted carriers retreat from Florida and Texas
summary: A continuation vehicle led by Lexington Partners and Barings poured more than $460 million into a catastrophe-exposed property managing general underwriter, capital meant to let it keep writing coverage in states where standard insurers are pulling back.

headline: ICICI Prudential Life seeks reclassification of Prudential as investor amid Bharti Life buyout
summary: As Prudential moves to take a 75% controlling stake in Bharti Life Insurance, ICICI Prudential Life's board asked regulators to reclassify Prudential Corporation Holdings from a promoter to an investor and is weighing a rename to ICICI Life, with both promoters signing a letter of undertaking on July 4 to manage the conflict of interest.

headline: High earners lean on HSAs over 401(k) catch-ups as new Roth mandate takes effect
summary: With 2026's requirement that catch-up contributions from workers earning over $150,000 be made on a Roth basis, advisors report high earners are increasingly prioritizing HSA contributions first for their triple tax advantage.

headline: India's hospital chains race to add capacity as Fortis breaks into Odisha
summary: Fortis Healthcare is building its first Odisha hospital, a roughly 300-bed, ₹500-crore tertiary care centre, part of a broader capacity expansion in which Apollo, Max and Fortis are together adding thousands of new beds nationwide.

headline: India's mutual fund industry posts record quarterly AUM on smaller-city SIP boom
summary: Average assets under management across India's mutual fund industry hit a fresh record of roughly ₹83.14 lakh crore in the April-June 2026 quarter, up more than 10% year-on-year, with over 40% of new SIPs now originating from smaller cities.

headline: Insurance investment outsourcing tops $5.5 trillion in third-party AUM as APAC allocations surge
summary: Third-party general-account assets under management placed with outside managers grew 23% year-on-year, with private insurance AUM more than doubling since 2021 to $947 billion as insurers chase private fixed income capabilities.

headline: Insurtech Insights 2026 shows industry moving from 'what is AI' to deployment questions
summary: At the 2026 Insurtech Insights conference, discussion shifted from explaining artificial intelligence to debating how agentic AI is actually being rolled out across underwriting and claims, along with real operational growing pains.

headline: RIA Roll-Up Wave Keeps Accelerating as National Platforms Snap Up Regional Advisory Shops
summary: National wealth platforms including Wealth Enhancement, Hightower and Aspen Standard Wealth continued a summer buying spree, absorbing firms such as an 88-year-old New York advisory practice and adding billions of dollars in combined client assets.

headline: U.S. P&C insurers' underwriting profits look to have peaked in 2025 as growth cools into 2026
summary: Industry analysis shows property-casualty insurers' returns hitting a high point in 2025, with premium growth expected to slow and competition intensifying as the softer-pricing cycle continues through 2026.

headline: Catastrophe bond issuance hit a record $18 billion in first half of 2026
summary: Artemis.bm reports 83 144A and private catastrophe bond transactions came to market in the first half of 2026, a new half-year notional record, as insurers and reinsurers lean further on capital markets for risk transfer.

headline: India's pension regulator loosens NPS exit and withdrawal rules for subscribers
summary: PFRDA notified amended regulations governing exits and withdrawals under the National Pension System, part of a broader push this year to give NPS subscribers more flexibility, including easier fund transfers and liquidity options against their balances.

headline: Northwell and Nuvance finalize merger, creating a $22.6 billion New York-Connecticut system
summary: Northwell Health completed its merger with Nuvance Health, forming a combined system of 28 hospitals and over 1,000 care sites with $22.6 billion in revenue and more than 100,000 employees.

headline: Allianz and Zurich launch joint blended-finance vehicle with government backers
summary: Allianz and Zurich, alongside AXA and Canadian pension giant La Caisse, launched Scaled Development, a platform meant to mobilize private capital for sustainable projects in emerging markets, with Germany and Canada committing initial public capital of up to €130 million.

headline: Steward Partners taps Sequoia Financial's Joseph Glick as new COO
summary: Steward Partners, which now oversees more than $53 billion in assets, hired Joseph Glick away from Sequoia Financial Group to run operations, technology and finance as the firm scales.

headline: SquareTrade launches licensed insurer entity in Brussels to reshape European strategy
summary: Warranty and protection-plan provider SquareTrade launched a newly licensed insurance entity in Brussels, bringing underwriting capabilities in-house as it accelerates growth across Europe.

headline: US fintech investment grows in Q2 2026 on 23% jump in larger deals
summary: US fintech investment increased in the second quarter of 2026, driven by a 23% quarter-over-quarter rise in larger funding rounds, signaling renewed investor appetite for scaled fintech platforms.

headline: London court clears Lloyd's and Arch of massive Nord Stream sabotage payout
summary: A UK court ruled that a war-risk exclusion shields Lloyd's and Arch from a roughly €580 million claim tied to the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions, finding the damage stemmed from the war in Ukraine rather than an insured peril.

headline: Global Commercial Insurance Rates Fall as Property Softening Outweighs US Casualty Pressure
summary: Marsh's latest Global Insurance Market Index shows worldwide commercial insurance rates dropping about 5% in the second quarter, driven by steep declines in property pricing that more than offset continued rate increases in US casualty lines.

headline: New federal bill would let RIA clients qualify as accredited investors through their advisor relationship
summary: Proposed legislation, the Informed Investor Access Act, would let clients of registered investment advisors be treated as accredited investors, opening access to private markets and drawing praise from wealth management trade groups.

headline: Unum cedes $3.8 billion long-term care block to Fortitude Re
summary: Unum Life Insurance Company of America agreed to cede individual long-term care policies representing $3.8 billion of statutory reserves to Fortitude Reinsurance, which will retrocede the biometric risk to a global reinsurer while Unum keeps handling claims administration.

headline: Tech-enabled MGA Bamboo rolls out budget homeowners product for harder-to-place homes
summary: Bamboo Insurance launched an Essential homeowners program aimed at price-sensitive buyers, designed to accept a broader range of properties, including older homes and those with prior claims, than many standard admitted-market policies allow.

headline: Shepherd Insurance names its first-ever CIO as agency doubles down on tech
summary: Indiana-based Shepherd Insurance created a chief information officer role for the first time and appointed Collin Hill to it, signaling a deeper push into technology-led operations as the agency keeps growing.

headline: Four in ten insurers now use AI in underwriting as straight-through processing rates jump
summary: A new industry report finds 40% of insurers are leveraging AI within underwriting, with timelines collapsing from three days to three minutes in some workflows, straight-through processing rising from 10-15% to 70-90%, and fraud detection improving over 30%.

headline: Allstate's SquareTrade launches licensed insurer in Brussels
summary: SquareTrade Europe, an Allstate company, launched a newly licensed insurer headquartered in Brussels to gain direct control over underwriting and speed product launches across its 15 European markets.

headline: SEC eyes easing political-donation restrictions on investment advisers
summary: The SEC's newly released 2026 rulemaking agenda includes a plan to amend its long-standing pay-to-play rule governing political contributions by investment advisers, part of a broader 38-item agenda that leans toward deregulation and wider retail access to private markets.

headline: Ardonagh Group launches Axiiem to digitize specialty insurance placement
summary: UK broking group Ardonagh unveiled Axiiem, a new digital trading platform meant to connect data, distribution and underwriting capacity so brokers and carriers can place specialty risks faster and more transparently.

headline: ICICI Prudential Life moves to drop 'Prudential' as UK parent pivots to Bharti Life stake
summary: ICICI Prudential Life's board approved renaming the insurer ICICI Life Insurance and reclassifying Prudential Corporation Holdings as an investor rather than a promoter, tied to Prudential's plan to buy 75% of Bharti Life Insurance from Bharti Enterprises.

headline: WealthAi and Flanks Partner to Clean Up Fragmented Advisor Data
summary: The two wealthtech vendors are combining AI-driven workflow automation with aggregated, compliant portfolio data to help wealth managers streamline front-to-back-office operations and cut costs.

headline: ANV Finalizes Purchase of London Wholesale Broker Iris Insurance Brokers
summary: ANV Group completed its acquisition of Iris Insurance Brokers, combining a Lloyd's wholesale brokerage, an intermediary platform and an MGA incubator to expand its UK and European specialty distribution reach.

headline: Gallagher Expands Western Canada Presence With Wilson M. Beck Acquisition
summary: Arthur J. Gallagher acquired Burnaby-based commercial broker Wilson M. Beck Insurance Services in a deal described as among the largest ever completed in the Canadian market, deepening its construction and surety practices.

headline: Fixed annuity rates hold near 15-year highs even as Fed easing looms
summary: Top multi-year guaranteed annuity rates are sitting around 6.3%, well above comparable CD yields, though brokers expect rates to soften gradually as the Federal Reserve continues cutting.

headline: Singapore regulator floats protected-cell structure to grow alternative risk transfer
summary: MAS opened a consultation on a protected cell company framework meant to let Singapore compete for captive insurance, insurance-linked securities and sovereign risk-pooling business, running through early August.

headline: France's KAPIA-RGI snaps up Cegid Assurex to widen personal insurance software suite
summary: KAPIA-RGI acquired Cegid Assurex Solutions, adding capabilities across annuities, provident benefits, retirement savings and tax-withholding administration to its personal insurance software offering in France.

headline: Hightower's acquisitive Signature Wealth unit lands three more advisory teams worth $5 billion
summary: Hightower's Signature Wealth division added Private Vista, Hightower Great Lakes and The McGuirk & De Nevi Group in a combined deal bringing roughly $5 billion in assets, pushing its year-to-date total past $25 billion added through conversions and acquisitions.

headline: Value-based Medicare tech firm Pearl Health raises $110 million to expand payer partnerships
summary: Pearl Health closed a $110 million raise, a $50 million equity round led by Andreessen Horowitz plus a $60 million credit facility, to grow its AI clinical intelligence platform used by providers and payers managing Medicare risk contracts.

headline: Swiss Re projects sharpest slowdown in global non-life premium growth in over a decade
summary: Swiss Re Institute forecasts real non-life premium growth will slow to just 0.6% in 2026, far below the 3.6% long-term trend, as competitive pricing and softer economic momentum weigh on advanced markets while insurer ROE eases from its 2025 peak.

headline: OpenAI leans on Sam Altman to court hospitals for its healthcare push
summary: OpenAI is pitching hospitals directly, with CEO Sam Altman personally engaging health systems, as the company rolls out ChatGPT for Clinicians and a consumer 'ChatGPT Health' feature while competing with Anthropic and Google for enterprise healthcare business.

headline: UK unveils new framework to cut heart disease and stroke deaths
summary: The UK government launched a Cardiovascular Disease Modern Service Framework setting 12 near-term priorities aimed at preventing thousands of premature heart disease and stroke deaths annually through earlier diagnosis and more consistent care.

headline: Singapore regulator floats protected cell company framework for alternative risk transfer
summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore opened a consultation on a new Protected Cell Company legislative structure meant to deepen alternative risk transfer and collateralized reinsurance activity in the city-state.

headline: CFC recruits former Direct Line chief Adam Winslow as group CEO
summary: Specialty MGA CFC named Adam Winslow, formerly group CEO of Direct Line Group, as its next chief executive, succeeding Louise O'Shea as the company looks to accelerate international growth and AI adoption.

headline: Hybrid RIA AmeriFlex reaches its $3 billion growth target six months ahead of schedule
summary: The AmeriFlex Group added 18 advisors and more than $1.7 billion in client assets in the first half of 2026, crediting succession-matching tools for pulling forward its annual growth goal.

headline: Independent agency Barge Group consolidates quoting on EZLynx's rating platform
summary: Barge Group adopted EZLynx's integrated personal-lines rater to enter risk data once and pull real-time quotes from multiple carriers, aiming to speed proposals and free up time for prospecting.

headline: Insurance Journal previews industry 'Demo Day' showcasing agentic AI underwriting tools
summary: Insurance Journal spotlighted an upcoming Risky Future event where vendors will demo agentic AI tools built for underwriting, part of a broader industry push to move AI pilots into production for policy pricing.

headline: Claims-communication insurtech Kyber named a 2026 PropertyCasualty360 Insurance Luminary
summary: Kyber was recognized in PropertyCasualty360's 2026 Insurance Luminaries class for workplace culture, with founder and CEO Arvind Sontha honored as Rising Star of the Year.

headline: NHS delayed hospital discharges now cost £2.7 billion a year, King's Fund finds
summary: Analysis from the King's Fund shows the cost of patients stuck in hospital beds despite being medically fit for discharge rose 7.5% in a year, driven by strained social care and community services capacity.

headline: NICE greenlights two non-invasive tests to cut years-long endometriosis diagnosis delays
summary: NICE recommended NHS use of Endotest, a saliva-based biomarker test, and EndoSure, a gut-signal sensor test, for a three-year evidence-gathering period aimed at speeding endometriosis diagnosis in primary care.

headline: Palantir expands AI partnership with Mexico's largest insurer GNP Seguros
summary: Palantir Technologies expanded its enterprise agreement with GNP Seguros, its first publicly announced commercial customer in Latin America, to scale Foundry and AI Platform use across health, life, motor and property lines for fraud detection and claims.

headline: Duck Creek buys London underwriting-AI firm Send to link core systems with intelligent risk decisioning
summary: Core P&C software provider Duck Creek Technologies acquired London-based Send Technology Solutions, an AI-native underwriting engine that supports more than $26 billion in premium for commercial, specialty and MGA business.

headline: MGAA sets 2026 priorities and confirms new board directors from Lloyd's, Aviva and member MGAs
summary: The Managing General Agents' Association outlined plans to expand member value and delegated-underwriting training, naming new elected and appointed directors including leaders from Lloyd's, Aviva and Optio Group.

headline: Principal Financial Group agrees to acquire employee-benefits TPA Beam Benefits
summary: Principal said it will acquire Beam Benefits, which administers employee benefits for more than 25,000 small businesses, to strengthen its position in the small and midsized business segment.

headline: Aspen Standard Wealth adds $1.3B Michigan RIA CWS Financial Advisors in its eighth deal
summary: The PE-backed RIA aggregator acquired Kalamazoo-based CWS Financial Advisors, which will keep its fee-only structure while joining the platform, pushing Aspen's total affiliated assets to $15 billion.

headline: Gallagher buys Western Canada retail brokerage Wilson M. Beck
summary: Arthur J. Gallagher acquired Burnaby, British Columbia-based Wilson M. Beck Insurance Services, adding a commercial brokerage with construction, real estate and hospitality specialties to its Canadian retail operations.

headline: UK's MGA trade body names Bspoke's Tim Smyth as new chairman
summary: The Managing General Agents' Association appointed Tim Smyth, who recently sold Bspoke Group to NFP (an Aon company), as its new chairman, succeeding Charles Manchester after his decade-long tenure.

headline: Pediatric primary-care platform Pediatrica lands $28 million to expand across the Sun Belt
summary: Miami-based Pediatrica Health Group, which operates pediatric primary-care practices across Florida and Texas, closed a $28 million Series B led by Valspring Capital that it plans to use for organic growth, acquisitions and investment in value-based care capabilities.

headline: Gallagher deepens Canadian presence by snapping up Western Canada commercial broker
summary: Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. acquired Burnaby, British Columbia-based Wilson M. Beck Insurance Services, a commercial brokerage focused on construction, real estate, surety and mining, continuing its steady pace of tuck-in acquisitions across North America.

headline: AI compliance startup Norm AI rockets to unicorn status with insurer-backed $120M round
summary: Norm AI, an agentic legal and regulatory compliance platform, closed a $120 million Series C led by Khosla Ventures at a $1.2 billion valuation, with insurance and financial heavyweights New York Life, TIAA and Vanguard among the backers helping automate compliance reviews for regulated industries.

headline: NYU Langone deploys real-time emergency department AI to flag overlooked high-risk diagnoses
summary: The health system's models continuously watch documentation, lab results and imaging in its emergency department, surfacing a nudge when a pattern suggests a diagnosis may be worth revisiting, aimed at countering anchoring bias.

headline: Compliance-AI startup Norm AI hits unicorn status with $120 million round
summary: Norm AI, which embeds regulatory and legal reasoning into AI agents for regulated enterprises, raised a $120 million Series C at a $1.2 billion valuation led by Khosla Ventures, with Vanguard, New York Life and TIAA also participating.

headline: Duck Creek Buys AI Underwriting Startup Send to Build Agentic Insurance Platform
summary: Duck Creek Technologies has acquired Send Technology Solutions, combining Duck Creek's core systems with Send's AI-native underwriting engine to create what it describes as the industry's first fully agentic policy lifecycle platform.

headline: EU clears Zurich's £8.1 billion takeover of Beazley
summary: The European Commission approved Zurich Insurance Group's all-cash acquisition of London-listed specialty insurer Beazley under simplified merger review, finding no competition concerns; the deal still awaits remaining regulatory sign-offs including from the UK's PRA.

headline: Gallagher Bassett leans on flexible adjuster model as severe weather strains claims volumes
summary: Facing a surge of complex, weather-driven claims, TPA giant Gallagher Bassett described shifting to an integrated field-and-desk adjusting model that lets it flex resources on demand, arguing that resilience and adaptability are becoming the differentiators for claims partners as catastrophe risk intensifies.

headline: Duck Creek Buys Underwriting Startup Send to Build an Agentic Insurance Platform
summary: Insurance software provider Duck Creek Technologies acquired Send Technology Solutions, an AI-native underwriting orchestration engine, to link policy administration with agentic underwriting workflows in what it describes as the industry's first combined offering of its kind.

headline: Zurich clears final EU antitrust hurdle for GBP8.1 billion Beazley takeover
summary: The European Commission approved Zurich Insurance Group's acquisition of Lloyd's insurer Beazley under simplified merger review; the all-cash deal still needs sign-off from UK, Swiss and Lloyd's regulators.

headline: SEC forms Retail Fraud Working Group to sharpen focus on advisor and broker misconduct
summary: The SEC's Division of Enforcement launched a new Retail Fraud Working Group to coordinate the agency's response to fraud targeting individual investors, including breaches of duty by investment advisers and broker-dealers.

headline: French brokertech Panora lands $5M seed to bring AI tools to European brokers
summary: Panora, a French startup building AI software for insurance brokers, raised a $5 million seed round led by Isai to expand its engineering team and AI agents, having already signed 40 broker clients across France, Belgium and the UK.

headline: Report Finds Insurers' Policy Wording Changes Are Quietly Reducing Claim Volumes
summary: New industry research shows shifts in coverage language and provisions are suppressing the number of claims filed, an underappreciated factor reshaping loss-cost trends across personal and commercial lines.

headline: Allianz Partners to cut up to 1,800 jobs as it leans further into AI
summary: Allianz's travel-and-assistance unit confirmed plans to eliminate as many as 1,800 European roles as part of a broader push to adopt AI across claims and customer service operations.

headline: ACA marketplace insurers propose another double-digit premium jump for 2027
summary: A KFF analysis of 77 insurers' rate filings found a median proposed 2027 ACA premium increase of 14%, following 2026's 20% median hike, driven by rising costs, regulatory changes and the expiration of enhanced subsidies.

headline: Alkeme pushes into MGA program underwriting with Virtue Risk buy
summary: Broker consolidator Alkeme acquired Virtue Risk Partners, marking its entry into managing general agent program underwriting and broadening its specialty distribution capabilities beyond retail brokerage.

headline: Agentic-AI vendor mea earns spot in Gartner's 2026 life insurance hype cycle
summary: Insurance-focused agentic AI company mea Platform was recognized in multiple independent 2026 industry research reports and awards, including being named in Gartner's Hype Cycle for Life Insurance 2026 for its document-processing and decisioning capabilities.

headline: Advisor-tech incumbents fight back with in-house AI tools
summary: Salesforce, RightCapital and YCharts each rolled out new AI features this month, including meeting notetakers and planning analyzers, as established platforms race to match standalone AI startups like Jump and Zocks rather than lose advisors to them.

headline: ALKEME Insurance acquires specialty MGA Virtue Risk Partners
summary: US brokerage ALKEME Insurance bought New York-based MGA Virtue Risk Partners, which underwrites casualty and environmental specialty coverage for contractors, consultants and engineers nationwide.

headline: Zhibao Technology extends embedded insurance to Chengdu's Tianfu Citizen's Cloud platform
summary: Zhibao's brokerage subsidiary launched a beta deployment putting embedded insurance products in front of more than 20 million new users through a Chinese municipal digital-services platform.

headline: Hyperscale data center boom strains property insurance capacity
summary: A construction wave of AI-driven data centers is testing insurers' appetite for large, complex property risk, pushing some carriers toward securitization structures to manage concentrated exposure.

headline: PBM trade group launches its largest-ever ad campaign as reform pressure builds in Washington
summary: The Pharmaceutical Care Management Association unveiled a seven-figure lobbying and advertising push framing drugmakers as the affordability problem, countering momentum for PBM reform following Congress's February legislation delinking PBM pay from drug list prices.

headline: Insurity deepens insurtech partnership with OIP for AI-driven document processing
summary: Insurity is expanding its multi-year partnership with OIP Insurtech, broadening the AI-enabled document intelligence and system-integration services it delivers to insurance carriers.

headline: India moves to let a cooperative-sector company sell life insurance
summary: India's cooperation minister said the government will facilitate a new cooperative-sector life insurer now that a legal change has removed a prior capital barrier, even as overall life insurance penetration has slipped for a third straight year.

headline: India's life insurers post 16% retail premium growth in June
summary: India's life insurance sector logged a 16% year-on-year jump in retail premiums for June 2026, led by state-owned LIC's 21% gain, while private insurers ICICI Prudential and SBI Life also posted strong double-digit growth in new business.

headline: LPL Financial keeps recruiting streak alive with a $6 billion hybrid RIA and two advisor teams
summary: LPL Financial added a roughly $6 billion hybrid RIA along with two additional advisor teams managing hundreds of millions in assets, underscoring intense competition among broker-dealer platforms for breakaway advisors.

headline: Hyperexponential launches agentic AI tool that turns broker submissions into priced quotes
summary: Hyperexponential introduced hyperoperator, an AI agent that moves commercial P&C broker submissions from initial intake to a decision-ready, priced file inside a carrier's existing pricing and authority controls — in one demo, pricing a cyber risk in under three minutes.

headline: Jointly AI launches what it calls the first fully autonomous AI insurance broker platform
summary: Jointly AI unveiled an end-to-end autonomous brokerage platform for UK personal-lines insurance that uses voice AI to call providers, navigate phone menus, negotiate quotes and deliver results without human involvement.

headline: Zhibao Technology scales embedded insurance to nearly 20 million users via China smart-city partnership
summary: Zhibao Technology expanded its embedded insurance ecosystem through a partnership with Tianfu Citizen's Cloud, a Chengdu smart-city services platform, extending digital insurance access to nearly 20 million registered users.

headline: IKS Health acquires health IT vendor TruBridge in $557 million deal
summary: IKS Health agreed to acquire TruBridge for $557 million, combining IKS's clinical documentation and revenue-cycle services with TruBridge's health IT platform as healthcare M&A activity remains elevated through 2026.

headline: SIAA-backed Sequel Insurance Agencies buys long-running Texas brokerage Watkins
summary: Sequel Insurance Agencies has acquired 76-year-old Watkins Insurance Group, adding five Austin-area and Central Texas offices and continuing a string of bolt-on acquisitions that push Sequel's network past $550 million in represented premium.

headline: Annuity sales are on pace for another record-setting year
summary: Industry coverage points to U.S. annuity sales staying above $450 billion in 2026 after four straight record years, with fixed indexed annuities and in-plan lifetime-income products cited as key growth drivers.

headline: Pearl Health raises $110 million to expand Medicare AI platform
summary: The value-based care technology company closed a $50 million Series C led by Andreessen Horowitz plus a $60 million credit facility, funding it will use to grow its AI-driven risk and workflow tools for providers managing Medicare patients.

headline: Big asset managers post solid June AUM gains as markets climb
summary: Invesco disclosed preliminary assets under management of about $2.47 trillion at the end of June 2026, up nearly 1% month over month, as peers including AllianceBernstein and Artisan Partners also reported higher managed assets heading into second-quarter earnings.

headline: FinTech Junction 2026 returns to Tel Aviv, drawing insurance, payments and AI leaders
summary: Israel's leading annual fintech conference brought together senior leaders from banking, insurance, cybersecurity, payments and the startup ecosystem for a day of programming aimed at enterprise decision-makers.

headline: Survey: 86% of underwriters more excited about their profession's future because of AI
summary: Research from Sixfold found the overwhelming majority of underwriting executives feel increasingly enthusiastic about the industry's direction as AI reshapes their day-to-day work.

headline: Vertafore adds new AI agent to automate MGA submission intake
summary: Vertafore introduced a Velocity AI Submission Processing Agent that reads emails, PDFs and spreadsheets to extract policy data for MGA workflows, reaching roughly 87% extraction accuracy in early trials and automatically flagging incomplete submissions.

headline: Swiss Re Institute says life insurance will lead global premium growth as rates stay elevated
summary: Swiss Re Institute's latest sigma report forecasts global life insurance premiums growing 2.3% in real terms in 2026, above the long-term trend, as higher yields keep supporting savings and annuity sales while emerging markets benefit from favorable demographics.

headline: AssuranceAmerica breach exposed 6.9 million driver's license records after 115-day notification delay
summary: Auto insurer AssuranceAmerica confirmed a breach traced to a compromised employee account in March that exposed names, driver's license numbers and policy details for roughly 6.9 million people, with notification letters only going out in mid-July.

headline: NYU Langone deploys real-time AI alerts in the emergency department to catch high-risk diagnoses
summary: NYU Langone's emergency department is running models that watch documentation, lab results and imaging in real time, surfacing alerts when patterns suggest a high-risk diagnosis may be worth revisiting to counter anchoring bias.

headline: North American life insurers show resilient earnings despite market turbulence, Morningstar DBRS finds
summary: Morningstar DBRS reports average adjusted earnings rose 10% quarter-over-quarter among the ten largest non-mutual North American life insurers, including MetLife, Prudential and Manulife, pointing to steady capital strength heading into the second half of 2026.

headline: UK Brokers Face Bigger-Than-Average Bill Hike to Fund Financial Regulator
summary: The FCA confirmed that insurance brokers' contribution to funding the regulator will rise faster than the watchdog's overall budget increase for 2026/27, following a consultation on fees and levies that drew industry pushback.

headline: Medicare-focused tech firm Pearl Health secures $110 million to scale AI risk tools
summary: Pearl Health raised a mix of equity and credit, led by Andreessen Horowitz and Trinity Capital, to expand its AI platform that helps providers manage Medicare and Medicare Advantage risk-based contracts.

headline: Lazard Asset Management's Hogbin reshapes the firm around AI and new hires
summary: Lazard Asset Management CEO Chris Hogbin is restructuring the firm with a wave of senior hires and a heavier bet on artificial intelligence tools, part of a broader push to reposition the asset manager competitively.

headline: MedPAC pegs Medicare Advantage overpayments at $76 billion this year
summary: MedPAC estimates Medicare Advantage plans will be overpaid by roughly $76 billion in 2026 relative to the cost of covering similar beneficiaries in traditional Medicare, even as MA now covers 55% of eligible beneficiaries.

headline: Recordkeepers Race to Bake AI Into Retirement Income Tools
summary: Major providers are rolling out AI-driven retirement income planning features with dynamic withdrawal strategies, though commentators note most asset managers still haven't incorporated AI into glidepath design or risk management for target-date defaults.

headline: ACA Marketplace Enrollment Drops Sharply After Enhanced Subsidies Expire
summary: With pandemic-era enhanced ACA subsidies gone as of January 2026, total marketplace enrollment fell roughly 12% year-over-year to about 19.2 million by February, with the steepest drop-off among higher-income enrollees now facing the return of the subsidy 'cliff.'

headline: Cyber-Focused MGA Trivora Lands Growth Investment From Carroll Street Capital
summary: Specialty cyber MGA Trivora secured a growth capital investment led by private equity firm Carroll Street Capital, giving it fresh funding to expand into additional specialty insurance lines.

headline: Fitch Warns US P&C Pricing Will Keep Softening as Competition Heats Up
summary: Fitch Ratings expects the U.S. property and casualty insurance market to soften further through 2026 as intensifying carrier competition and growing capacity pressure pricing, particularly in property lines.

headline: Swiss Re projects global insurance premium growth will slow sharply to 1.3% in 2026
summary: Swiss Re Institute's latest World Insurance sigma report projects global real premium growth slowing to about 1.3% in 2026 from 3.9% in 2025, with non-life growth nearly flat as pricing competition intensifies and life premiums outperforming the long-term trend.

headline: InsuranceDekho's parent lines up bankers for a $400 million India listing
summary: Girnar Insurance Brokers, the entity behind insurance aggregator InsuranceDekho and backed by Investcorp and BNP Paribas Cardif, has reportedly picked HSBC, Morgan Stanley, ICICI Securities and IIFL Capital to advise on a planned IPO that could raise up to $400 million.

headline: Arrow Global acquires specialist MGA Fusion Specialty Group
summary: Pan-European investment manager Arrow Global bought MGA Fusion Specialty Group through its insurance unit, adding an established London-market underwriting franchise to its growing MGA platform.

headline: Roadzen to Buy European Car-Rental Insurance MGA for $15 Million
summary: Nasdaq-listed insurtech Roadzen signed a deal to acquire a technology-driven European MGA focused on short-term car rental insurance, adding roughly 800,000 policies a year and AI-based underwriting and claims tools to its platform.

headline: NHS logs its busiest-ever month as heatwaves and World Cup crowds push A&E demand to record highs
summary: Average daily A&E attendances topped 81,000 for the first time in June as temperatures hit nearly 38C, with NHS leaders warning that summer is now straining the health service as much as winter historically has.

headline: Gallagher expands wholesale reach with acquisition of Kansas MGA Med James
summary: Arthur J. Gallagher's Risk Placement Services wholesale unit acquired Overland Park-based Med James, a managing general agency and wholesale broker, extending Gallagher's binding-authority footprint in the North Central US.

headline: Global wealthtech investment sinks 67% year-over-year even as deal count climbs
summary: Wealthtech startups worldwide raised roughly $932 million across 151 deals in the second quarter of 2026, a sharp drop in dollars from a year earlier despite a 10% rise in deal volume, with the US capturing about half of the period's top ten rounds.

headline: Arrow Global Group agrees to acquire specialty MGA Fusion Specialty Group
summary: Arrow Global Group announced an agreement to acquire Fusion Specialty Group, a specialist managing general agent, in a deal expected to close in the third quarter of 2026 subject to regulatory approval.

headline: US P&C industry posts $16.3 billion Q1 underwriting gain as catastrophe losses plunge
summary: The U.S. property and casualty industry swung to a $16.3 billion net underwriting gain in the first quarter of 2026, reversing a year-ago loss, as catastrophe losses fell to $10 billion from $33.3 billion a year earlier following the 2025 California wildfires.

headline: Arrow Global expands into specialty lines with Fusion Specialty MGA purchase
summary: Arrow Global Group announced it is acquiring Fusion Specialty Group, a specialist managing general agent, as part of a broader push by credit and asset manager Arrow into specialty insurance distribution. The deal adds underwriting and distribution capability to Arrow's existing financial services platform.

headline: Principal Financial buys dental-benefits insurtech Beam in a sign M&A appetite is back
summary: Principal Financial Group agreed to acquire Beam Benefits, a technology-driven dental and vision insurance provider, in a deal that industry watchers say shows the employer health-benefits M&A market remains active despite a broader slowdown in insurance dealmaking.

headline: Corebridge and Equitable shareholders to vote on $22 billion merger this month
summary: Corebridge Financial and Equitable Holdings have scheduled special shareholder meetings for July 30 to approve their previously announced all-stock combination, which would create a retirement, life and asset management group with roughly $1.5 trillion in assets under the Equitable name.

headline: Asset manager Arrow Global buys into the MGA boom with Fusion Specialty deal
summary: Alternative investment firm Arrow Global Group agreed to acquire UK-based Fusion Specialty Group to expand its specialty insurance platform, part of a broader wave of private capital flowing into managing general agents as rates in some lines firm.

headline: Compliance-AI startup Norm AI raises $120 million, crosses unicorn threshold
summary: Norm AI closed a $120 million Series C led by Khosla Ventures at a $1.2 billion valuation, reaching unicorn status less than three years after founding.

headline: Asset managers push to expand 401(k) menus to include private-market investments
summary: Wall Street firms are lobbying to widen the range of alternative and private-asset investments permitted inside 401(k) plans, a shift critics warn could raise fee and liquidity risks for retirement savers.

headline: Viz.ai expands into neurodegenerative disease with Cortechs.ai tie-up
summary: Viz.ai will integrate Cortechs.ai's quantitative neuroimaging tools into its care-coordination platform, starting with multiple sclerosis, giving hospitals in its roughly 2,000-site US network faster ways to identify and manage MS patients.

headline: Hightower agrees to acquire $9.5 billion RIA The Bahnsen Group
summary: Hightower signed a deal to acquire The Bahnsen Group, a 12-office RIA overseeing roughly $9.5 billion in assets across 10 states, in a transaction expected to close in the third quarter of 2026 as consolidation among independent advisory firms continues.

headline: IRDAI moves to spread insurance agent commissions across a policy's full term
summary: India's insurance regulator is preparing a consultation paper proposing that distributor commissions, currently front-loaded and as high as 40% of premium, be paid out over the life of a policy to curb mis-selling and reward ongoing customer service.

headline: RIAs and wirehouses brace for a fresh round of regulatory change in 2026
summary: Advisory firms across the RIA and wirehouse channels are tracking a slate of potential regulatory shifts this year, prompting compliance teams to reassess policies around fees, disclosures and advisor mobility.

headline: IRDAI weighs shift to trail-based commissions to curb insurance mis-selling
summary: India's insurance regulator is considering replacing large upfront agent commissions with payouts staggered over a policy's life and linked to persistency, with a consultation paper expected by the end of July 2026.

headline: Vertafore rolls out AI agent to speed up MGA submission intake
summary: Insurance technology provider Vertafore launched an AI-powered submission processing agent that pulls structured data from unstructured broker submissions like emails and PDFs, aiming to cut manual intake work for managing general agents, with early users reporting roughly 87% accuracy.

headline: Colorado shifts workers' comp claims reporting to new EDI 3.1 standard for carriers and TPAs
summary: Colorado's Division of Workers' Compensation moved its electronic data interchange requirement to the newer EDI 3.1 format in July, requiring carriers and third-party administrators to update claims-submission systems.

headline: Gallagher's wholesale unit RPS buys Kansas MGA Med James to extend reach across six states
summary: Arthur J. Gallagher's wholesale brokerage arm Risk Placement Services acquired Med James, an Overland Park, Kansas-based MGA focused on property-casualty and transportation risks, continuing a string of wholesale tuck-in deals.

headline: Health insurer stocks climb as Wall Street braces for a closely watched Q2 2026 earnings season
summary: Investors are watching CVS and peers for signs of whether the industry can sustain the earnings beats and raised guidance most major insurers delivered in Q1, after medical cost ratios came in better than analysts feared.

headline: Vestmark's RIA advisory assets jump to $50 billion from $10 billion in 18 months
summary: Vestmark Advisory Services has grown the assets it manages for RIAs five-fold in a year and a half, crediting referral relationships with major asset managers and demand for its tax-overlay and direct-indexing technology.

headline: Willis reshuffles Asia leadership with new Southeast Asia and regional commercial chiefs
summary: Willis (WTW) named Oliver Pryce as Head of Corporate Risk & Broking for Southeast Asia and Rupert Roberts as Chief Commercial Officer for Asia, both moves aimed at sharpening the broker's regional growth strategy. The appointments are part of a wider set of senior moves across the brokerage as competition for Asian corporate risk business intensifies.

headline: Singapore and China deepen ties on medical AI as regional health-tech forum convenes
summary: Chinese and Singaporean health professionals gathered around the theme of designing an AI-driven healthcare future, part of a broader push across the Asia-Pacific region to close gaps in hospital adoption of AI-based diagnosis and remote-monitoring tools even as strategic investment in digital health infrastructure accelerates.

headline: Direct lenders close some of the largest private credit funds on record in first-half 2026
summary: A first-half fundraising roundup shows managers including Barings, Crescent Capital, Churchill Asset Management and Blackstone closing multibillion-dollar direct-lending and credit vehicles, reflecting insurers' and institutions' rising appetite for private credit.

headline: MetLife signals softer alternative-investment returns for the second quarter
summary: MetLife issued a preliminary estimate putting second-quarter 2026 variable investment income - largely returns from private equity and real estate funds - well below its full-year guidance pace, a cautious signal for insurers' alternative asset portfolios.

headline: AI-focused startups capture 97% of disclosed insurtech funding in H1 2026
summary: The Simon-Kucher Insurtech Tracker found AI-focused companies took in $820 million, or 97% of all disclosed insurtech funding, in the first half of 2026, as investor attention shifts from purchase-flow digitization to rebuilding insurers' operating infrastructure.

headline: Assured Guaranty enters annuity reinsurance market via Warwick Re deal
summary: Bond insurer Assured Guaranty is expanding into annuity reinsurance through the acquisition of Bermuda-based Warwick Re, marking its first move into the life and annuity reinsurance space.

headline: Pooled employer plans become recordkeepers' main growth engine for 2026
summary: Cerulli research finds 60% of retirement recordkeepers now offer pooled employer plan (PEP) services, with firms expecting PEPs to drive 20-40% of new business growth this year as the structure moves from niche to mainstream.

headline: UK bulk annuity market tracking toward record £70 billion of pension risk transfer in 2026
summary: Advisers expect UK defined-benefit schemes to transfer roughly £50 billion via buy-ins and buyouts plus £20 billion of longevity swaps this year, with more than 150,000 members moving into individual annuity contracts.

headline: MISSION-backed Amulet Specialty launches as a new property and casualty MGA
summary: Amulet Specialty, a new specialist MGA backed by MISSION and led by co-founders Paul Bennett and Jonathan Dermody, launched offering property, casualty, liability and business-interruption cover.

headline: DOL urges Supreme Court to uphold dismissal of Intel 401(k) alternative-assets suit
summary: The Department of Labor filed an amicus brief backing a stricter pleading standard and asking the Supreme Court to affirm dismissal of a lawsuit accusing Intel of imprudently investing its 401(k) plan in non-traditional assets like private equity and hedge funds.

headline: Aon hires WTW's Sean Deehan to lead APAC strategy and technology
summary: Aon appointed Sean Deehan, formerly WTW's Greater China divisional leader, as CEO of its Strategy and Technology Group for Asia-Pacific, tasked with expanding adoption of Aon's PathWise life-and-annuity risk modeling platform across the region.

headline: Nearly 5 million could lose coverage as enhanced ACA subsidies lapse
summary: With enhanced ACA premium tax credits expired and congressional extension stalled, the Urban Institute projects roughly 4.8 million people will become uninsured in 2026 as marketplace premiums rise sharply for many enrollees.

headline: 401(k) recordkeepers lean into AI modernization as a fight over participant data looms
summary: Facing fee pressure, retirement recordkeepers are investing in AI-driven automation and faster processing to improve participant service, even as the industry heads toward disputes over who can access and monetize participant data.

headline: SEC's New Regulatory Agenda Signals Looser Marketing Rules but Sharper Scrutiny of Advisers
summary: The SEC's freshly published 2026 rulemaking agenda proposes reworking the adviser pay-to-play rule, opening a path for retail investors into private markets, and clarifying custody rules for crypto assets, while regulators keep tightening focus on adviser conduct and marketing practices.

headline: ANV Group Buys Broker Iris to Broaden Its UK Distribution and MGA Reach
summary: ANV Group acquired UK insurance broker Iris in a move designed to expand its distribution footprint and strengthen its managing general agent platform in the British market.

headline: AI-Driven Pay-Per-Mile MGA Buys Up Legacy Agency as Carriers Scrutinize Distribution Ties
summary: Mile Auto, an AI-powered managing general agency, acquired Insurance House effective July 1, creating a combined operation with close to $100 million in annual premium, over 55,000 policyholders and roughly 1,600 independent agency relationships across ten states.

headline: India's insurance regulator weighs tying agent payouts to how long policies stay in force
summary: IRDAI is reportedly exploring rules that would connect distributor commissions to policyholder persistency, an effort meant to discourage churn-driven sales and cut down on early policy lapses.

headline: States move to force disclosure of private-equity hospital buyouts
summary: With private equity firms now owning close to one in ten U.S. private hospitals, a growing number of states have begun requiring pre-closing notification and public review of PE-led hospital transactions, including ownership and financing details.

headline: Recordkeepers double down on pooled employer plans as adoption tops 50,000 employers
summary: More than 50,000 employers have now joined a pooled employer plan, with 58% of recordkeepers already administering PEPs and another 17% planning to within a year, as the model becomes a bigger part of the DC plan landscape.

headline: Gallagher's RPS unit acquires Kansas wholesaler Med James
summary: Arthur J. Gallagher's wholesale brokerage arm, Risk Placement Services, acquired Overland Park, Kansas-based Med James, a roughly 50-employee MGA focused on property/casualty, transportation and excess liability risk, extending RPS's wholesale footprint in the North Central region.

headline: Blue Cross NC to return as North Carolina State Health Plan's TPA, replacing Aetna
summary: North Carolina's State Health Plan trustees voted to bring back Blue Cross NC as third-party administrator starting in 2028, ending Aetna's tenure after plan officials cited service concerns.

headline: Alan's $550M round anchors a record first half for European insurtech funding
summary: French insurtech Alan's $550 million raise accounted for more than a third of all InsurTech funding in the first half of 2026, as the sector's H1 total already topped 2025's full-year figure at roughly $1.54 billion across 27 deals.

headline: Insurtech investment pivots toward commercial and specialty lines as climate-risk startups gain ground
summary: InsurTech capital is increasingly flowing to commercial insurance, specialty coverage and professional broker software rather than consumer apps, with climate and property-risk startups such as Arbol and Understory drawing investor interest.

headline: Insurtech sector now counts nearly 7,920 active companies, with 3,080 having raised funding
summary: Tracking of the global insurtech landscape shows 7,919 active companies as of July 2026, with 3,080 of them having received outside funding, underscoring how the sector has broadened well beyond its early consumer-app roots.

headline: Target-date fund assets swell to $4.8 trillion, still concentrated among five firms
summary: The target-date fund industry grew 20.3% in 2025 to reach $4.8 trillion, with Vanguard alone holding roughly 37% of assets even as the broader industry keeps compounding at double-digit rates.

headline: BrokerTech Ventures and ManchesterStory launch dedicated broker-tech venture fund
summary: BrokerTech Ventures partnered with ManchesterStory to launch the BrokerTech Fund, the first venture capital vehicle targeting technology startups built specifically for insurance brokers and wholesalers.

headline: Hospitals create new AI-focused clinical leadership roles
summary: Health systems including UCI Health and Providence named their first chief medical informatics and AI officers this year, reflecting a broader wave of hospitals adding dedicated C-suite roles to govern clinical AI deployment.

headline: RIA dealmaking tops $100 billion of AUM in motion through Q2 2026
summary: A wave of large platform transactions, including LPL/Private Advisor Group's acquisition of the $31 billion Mariner Advisor Network and Mesirow's purchase of LeafHouse Financial Advisors, is driving RIA M&A volumes even as deal count growth moderates.

headline: Ellevest raises planning fees a third as advisor pricing climbs industrywide
summary: Women-focused RIA Ellevest lifted its annual financial planning fee from $3,600 to $4,800 and dropped monthly billing, part of a broader industry trend of rising advisor retainer fees.

headline: Plan Sponsors Face Year-End Deadline to Lock In SECURE Act Amendments
summary: Employers must formally adopt required SECURE Act, CARES Act and SECURE 2.0 plan amendments by December 31, 2026, even as newer rules such as mandatory Roth catch-up contributions for higher earners and paper-statement mandates are already taking effect.

headline: Tata Asset Management promotes longtime insider Vardarajan to top job
summary: Tata Asset Management named Anand Vardarajan, previously its chief business officer, as CEO and managing director effective July 10, 2026, succeeding Prathit Bhobe, while also elevating Hemant Kumar to chief business officer in the same leadership shuffle.

headline: US P&C insurers post $15.8 billion Q1 underwriting gain, reversing year-ago loss
summary: Private US property/casualty insurers swung to a first-quarter 2026 underwriting profit of $15.8 billion, a sharp turnaround from the $864 million underwriting loss recorded in the same period last year.

headline: Industry group pitches a centralized clearinghouse to stop 401(k) plan-hopping losses
summary: Retirement Clearinghouse proposed a centralized system connecting recordkeepers so small retirement balances automatically follow workers who change jobs, aiming to curb the cash-outs and lost accounts common across a typical career's 12-15 job changes.

headline: ACA premium spike pushes more shoppers into high-deductible bronze plans, CMS data show
summary: Healthcare Dive reports new CMS marketplace data show rising 2026 ACA premiums are driving more enrollees toward high-deductible bronze plans as enhanced subsidies shrink.
