headline: Global insurtech investment outpaces all of 2025 within just two quarters
summary: Global insurtech funding reached roughly $1.54 billion across 27 disclosed deals through the first half of 2026, already surpassing full-year 2025 totals, with AI-focused startups and later-stage follow-on rounds capturing the bulk of capital. North America led both deal count and dollars raised, while Europe's total was buoyed by a small number of large financings.

headline: Digital health funding rebounds to $7.4B in 2026 on AI wave
summary: Venture funding for digital health startups is climbing again in 2026, powered by an AI-driven rebound, with megadeals for companies like Whoop, OpenEvidence and Aidoc and AI-branded startups capturing more than half of all capital invested.

headline: Mercer survey finds asset managers' AI adoption real but still uneven
summary: Mercer's 2026 AI in Asset Management survey found 55% of asset managers have integrated AI into at least one investment process, 27% remain at the pilot stage, and just 18% report full integration across operations.

headline: ICI data shows US retirement assets holding near record levels entering 2026
summary: The Investment Company Institute's quarterly retirement market report shows total US retirement assets remaining near record highs, underscoring continued strength in defined-contribution plan balances.

headline: Women who work with a financial advisor report far higher retirement confidence
summary: New survey data cited in Kitces' weekend roundup found women working with a financial advisor are roughly 60% more likely to feel confident managing their finances, with retirement planning topping the list of areas where they seek professional help.

headline: Japan pushes its $1.8 trillion pension giant to triple alternative-asset exposure
summary: Japanese officials are urging GPIF, the world's largest pension fund, to lift allocations to private equity, real estate, credit and infrastructure from about 1.7% toward a 5% target as part of a broader overhaul of its investment strategy.

headline: Pooled employer plans become a top growth bet for 401(k) recordkeepers
summary: A new Cerulli report finds recordkeepers expect pooled employer plans to drive a growing share of new business, with adoption already up sharply year-over-year and most recordkeepers now supporting PEPs as a strategic priority.

headline: Baptist Health Arkansas set to close acquisition of Magnolia Regional Medical Center
summary: Baptist Health's transaction to acquire Magnolia Regional Medical Center was expected to close July 12, extending a run of hospital consolidation that has produced the strongest first-quarter deal count since 2020.

headline: Zurich reshuffles Asia Pacific commercial insurance leadership
summary: Zurich Insurance Group named Sean Walker head of commercial insurance and chief technical officer for Asia Pacific and hired Liam Burrell from AIG as head of commercial insurance for Asia and Singapore CEO, as the carrier builds out its regional commercial business.

headline: Underwriting automation funding jumps more than twentyfold year-over-year
summary: Underwriting automation startups raised roughly $178 million across seven deals so far in 2026, up sharply from about $8 million across two deals in the same period last year, per a weekly investment tracker.

headline: P&C market splits in two directions: property rates soften while casualty lines keep hardening
summary: Property insurance pricing is easing after a muted catastrophe year and a wave of reinsurance capital, even as casualty lines continue to harden under pressure from social inflation, larger jury awards and aggressive litigation funding.

headline: Independent agents placed 62% of all US P&C premium in 2025, up from 61.5%
summary: The Big 'I' 2026 Market Share Report shows independent agents wrote 62% of all property/casualty premium in the U.S. last year, including 87.7% of commercial lines, extending the channel's steady gains over captive and direct distribution.

headline: Broker Investment Group adds group COO to oversee retail and MGA integration
summary: The Broker Investment Group brought on Stuart Grieb as group chief operating officer effective July 13, giving him responsibility for operational execution across both its retail broking and MGA businesses. A second hire, Rosie Guru, joins the following week as group integration director, bringing transformation experience from RSA and NFP to support the group's consolidation strategy.

headline: India's fintech funding more than doubles quarter-on-quarter on jump in mega-deals
summary: Fintech investment in India climbed roughly 2.3 times sequentially in the second quarter of 2026, driven largely by a rise in deals exceeding $100 million, according to newly published funding data.

headline: Lockton stacks up senior specialty hires in Singapore to build out its Asia bench
summary: Broker Lockton has made six senior appointments across Asia since June, including a regional cyber advisory head and a marine and transportation growth leader based in Singapore, as it builds a specialty platform to compete for complex regional risks.

headline: UnitedHealth, Centene and Elevance post recovering quarterly results
summary: All three major payers beat earnings expectations in their latest quarter, with analysts pointing to improved medical-cost management and stabilizing Medicaid and ACA margins as evidence of a broader insurer rebound after a rough 2025.

headline: Insurity names Jatin Atre as CEO, succeeding Jeff Clarke
summary: Insurance software provider Insurity appointed Jatin Atre, previously its president since January, as chief executive officer; outgoing CEO Jeff Clarke moves to executive chairman as the company continues a $50 million AI R&D push.

headline: Malibu Life Holdings completes TruSpire acquisition, launching U.S. annuity arm
summary: London-listed insurance holding company Malibu Life Holdings closed its purchase of TruSpire Retirement Insurance Company, rebranding it Malibu Life USA to serve as its origination platform for the U.S. retail annuity market, with an inaugural product launch targeted for September.

headline: Mile Auto acquires Georgia MGA Insurance House to expand pay-per-mile platform
summary: The AI-driven pay-per-mile auto insurance MGA completed its acquisition of six-decade-old Insurance House effective July 1, creating a combined operation with nearly $100 million in annual premium across 1,600 agencies.

headline: Sedgwick earns Great Place To Work certification for fifth consecutive year
summary: The claims and TPA giant said the certification is based entirely on feedback from current employees about their experience working at the company.

headline: P&C insurers expand vendor technology stacks, latest carrier roundup shows
summary: PropertyCasualty360's latest 'who's using what' roundup tracks new technology vendor selections across property and casualty carriers, with Duck Creek Technologies featured among the most active platform providers this month.

headline: UK pensions regulator finalizes CDC rules while pressing schemes on dashboard readiness
summary: The Pensions Regulator's updated code supporting multi-employer collective defined contribution schemes takes effect July 31, 2026, alongside continued enforcement pressure on trustees to prepare data ahead of the October 31 pensions dashboards connection deadline.

headline: Wealth fintech Arca emerges from stealth with $64 million to build AI-powered advisory platform
summary: Arca, founded by a former Plaid product lead, raised a combined $64 million seed and Series A round led by Venrock and General Catalyst to build AI agents meant to support human financial advisors across planning, tax and estate work.

headline: PIB Group names Alastair Hay as chief financial officer
summary: UK-based insurance intermediary PIB Group appointed Alastair Hay as its new chief financial officer effective immediately, part of a wave of senior leadership moves across European brokers and MGAs in mid-July.

headline: Jensten Group deepens Scottish footprint by snapping up Kelvin Smith Insurance
summary: UK broking consolidator Jensten Group agreed to buy Glasgow-based Kelvin Smith Insurance, a broker with roughly £22 million in premium and 3,000-plus clients, extending its third Scottish acquisition in recent years.

headline: Optum taps Anthropic's Claude to automate claims and revenue-cycle work
summary: Optum unveiled a strategic tie-up with Anthropic to weave the Claude model into everyday insurance operations, targeting faster claims adjudication and less manual paperwork while keeping clinicians in the decision loop.

headline: Swiss Re warns current soft P&C cycle may be shallower than past downturns
summary: Swiss Re research suggests the ongoing softening in global property-casualty pricing could be less steep than prior soft markets, as rising repair costs and growing catastrophe losses limit how far rates can fall.

headline: Hospital dealmaking hits its busiest second quarter in years despite reimbursement uncertainty
summary: Hospitals and health systems recorded 18 M&A transactions in the second quarter of 2026, among the highest quarterly totals since 2018 and including three mega-mergers, according to a new Kaufman Hall report, suggesting consolidation momentum is holding up even as providers navigate reimbursement and policy uncertainty.

headline: Analysts warn under-governed AI models could become insurers' next compliance headache
summary: A trade analysis cautioned that insurers scaling AI across underwriting, claims and customer service without strong data governance risk inconsistent decisions and regulatory scrutiny as oversight of AI tightens worldwide.

headline: Malaysian insurtech PolicyStreet tops up Series C to $26 million with impact investor BlueOrchard
summary: Southeast Asian insurtech PolicyStreet added $5 million more to its Series C round, bringing the total to $26 million, with new backing from impact investor BlueOrchard to fund regional expansion into mobility, travel and gig-economy insurance.

headline: Carriers reposition AI as a loss-prevention tool, not just a pricing engine
summary: Insurance executives are increasingly framing artificial intelligence's biggest payoff as helping policyholders avoid losses before they happen, rather than only sharpening how underwriters price and select risk.

headline: Independent advisory firm Modera brings in new investment and operations chiefs
summary: Modera Wealth Management named a new chief investment officer and chief operating officer, both wealth management veterans, as the RIA looks to expand its investment offerings and modernize its technology platform.

headline: ACA marketplace insurers propose median 14% premium hike for 2027
summary: Preliminary filings from 77 ACA marketplace insurers across 16 states show a median proposed premium increase of 14% for 2027, the second-highest requested rate change since 2018, driven by rising medical costs and the expiration of enhanced premium tax credits.

headline: Wave of insurers sue CMS over 2026 Medicare Advantage Star ratings recalculation
summary: Alignment Healthcare and SCAN filed new suits against CMS seeking higher Medicare Advantage Star ratings, joining a wider wave of litigation that followed Clover Health's May court win over how CMS calculated quality measures.

headline: UCSF Health launches AI accelerator with Kleiner Perkins and Doerr Capital
summary: UCSF Health, Kleiner Perkins and Doerr Capital unveiled "UCSF Health Converge," an accelerator embedding startups with clinicians and operators inside the academic health system to build and validate AI tools in live care settings.

headline: UK regulators unveil plans for internationally competitive captive insurance regime
summary: The PRA and FCA laid out proposals on July 14 for a new UK captive insurance framework aimed at stopping domestic corporations from setting up captives overseas, with a formal launch targeted for 2027.

headline: KKR joins Amwins-Dragoneer consortium bidding for Australia's Steadfast in A$7.7 billion buyout
summary: Global investment firm KKR joined the existing takeover consortium pursuing insurance broker network Steadfast Group, with the group's due diligence period extended by four weeks and the A$6-per-share offer unchanged.

headline: Jensten Group expands into Scotland with Kelvin Smith Insurance acquisition
summary: UK broking group Jensten agreed to buy Glasgow-based Kelvin Smith Insurance, a broker founded in 1982 managing roughly £22 million of gross written premium, adding 30 staff and more than 3,000 clients as part of its Scottish expansion.

headline: Aon: APAC transaction-risk insurance claims grow more severe and complex
summary: Aon's 2026 Global Transaction Solutions Claims Study found Asia-Pacific M&A insurance claims increasingly involve high-severity, cross-border losses exceeding $10 million, with capacity and adoption expanding in India, Singapore and Korea.

headline: Guaranteed lifetime income tied to longer lifespans, NBER study finds
summary: New National Bureau of Economic Research analysis found retirees who convert savings into annuity income are about 3% less likely to die over the following decade than those who manage withdrawals on their own.

headline: MSIG Asia names Ronak Shah as regional chief executive
summary: MSIG Asia appointed insurance veteran Ronak Shah, most recently CEO of QBE's Wholesale Markets Asia business, as regional CEO effective October 1, succeeding Clemens Philippi.

headline: DOL disclosure proposal would apply to TPAs contracting with self-funded plans
summary: A Department of Labor proposal issued January 30 would require PBMs and third-party administrators to give employer-sponsored, self-funded ERISA health plans extensive advance fee and compensation disclosures before contracting, with proposed applicability starting July 1, 2026.

headline: New federal law forces PBMs and TPAs to open their books on fees
summary: Provisions in the 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act require pharmacy benefit managers and third-party administrators to disclose, at the claim level, the gap between what health plans pay them and what they reimburse pharmacies.

headline: Reliance Global Group launches in-house AI agent for insurance back-office automation
summary: Nasdaq-listed Reliance Global Group unveiled a proprietary AI agent that automates browser-based back-office tasks like endorsements, quote pulls and status checks for its network of insurance agencies, built with a compliance-focused security framework.

headline: Cover Genius raises $100 million at $1.9 billion valuation to scale embedded protection
summary: Embedded-insurance platform Cover Genius secured $100 million from Vista Credit Partners, pushing its valuation to $1.9 billion as it invests in AI-driven hyper-personalization and expands into new verticals.

headline: Hanwha Asset Management tilts H2 target-date strategy toward AI winners while urging diversification
summary: Hanwha Asset Management unveiled a second-half target-date fund strategy that raises exposure to companies benefiting from expanded AI investment, while cautioning Korean retirement savers to keep portfolios diversified.

headline: Specialty Insurer Canopius Poaches BCG Partner to Run Its US Business
summary: Canopius Group named Nadine Moore, a former senior partner at Boston Consulting Group, as CEO of its US operations starting in September, succeeding Lisa Davis as the London-based specialty carrier pushes to scale its American retail and wholesale business.

headline: KKR joins consortium's A$7.7 billion bid to take Australian broker Steadfast private
summary: KKR joined Amwins Group and Dragoneer Investment Group's non-binding proposal to acquire Australian insurance broker Steadfast Group for roughly A$7.7 billion, with KKR and Dragoneer set to control the retail brokerage business and Amwins taking the underwriting agency operations.

headline: Cover Genius raises $100 million credit facility at $1.9 billion valuation
summary: Embedded insurance platform Cover Genius closed a $100 million credit raise backed by Vista Credit Partners at a $1.9 billion valuation, a sign that embedded insurance financing has matured beyond traditional venture capital rounds.

headline: FTC secures Caremark settlement locking in up to $8.5 billion in consumer drug savings
summary: The Federal Trade Commission reached a settlement with Caremark Rx and Zinc Health Services resolving claims that the PBM used anticompetitive rebate schemes to inflate insulin prices, requiring rebate pass-through at the point of sale and estimated to save consumers up to $8.5 billion over a decade.

headline: Workers'-comp claims administrator ESIS accused of blowing past mandated bill-response deadlines
summary: A billing-compliance watchdog reported that TPA ESIS repeatedly failed to respond to electronic medical bills within legally required timeframes for an injured worker's claim, renewing scrutiny of TPA compliance with state reporting rules.

headline: Malaysia's PolicyStreet tops up funding round to $26M with impact investor backing
summary: Embedded-insurance player PolicyStreet added $5 million from BlueOrchard's climate-resilience strategy to its Series C, bringing the round to $26 million as it expands digital insurance distribution across Southeast Asia and Australia.

headline: ACA exchange enrollment plunges by 2.6 million as enhanced subsidies lapse
summary: Federal figures show marketplace sign-ups fell from roughly 21.8 million to 19.2 million year over year, the steepest drop since the exchanges launched, as expired premium tax credits push out-of-pocket costs sharply higher for many enrollees.

headline: North American broker M&A slumps to weakest first half since 2016
summary: Deal volume among P&C agents, brokers, benefits firms, MGAs and TPAs in the US and Canada fell about 15% to 292 transactions in H1 2026, the slowest pace in a decade as buyer-seller valuation gaps only partly narrowed.

headline: Mega-RIA Creative Planning buys Lovell Insurance Group to build out commercial insurance arm
summary: Creative Planning acquired Kansas City-based Lovell Insurance Group, giving the giant RIA in-house commercial insurance, surety and risk-management capabilities as it continues bolting specialized services onto its wealth platform.

headline: Macquarie-backed Enterprise Risk Associates acquires Florida's Insurance Solutions of America
summary: Enterprise Risk Associates, an insurance brokerage holding company backed by $150 million from Macquarie Capital, acquired Oviedo, Florida-based Insurance Solutions of America, a commercial brokerage specializing in fire suppression and life-safety risks, as it continues its agency-acquisition growth strategy.

headline: US P&C insurers post best underwriting result in a decade in 2025
summary: The U.S. property/casualty industry recorded a combined ratio of 93 in 2025, its best in ten years, as direct premiums written grew 5% to roughly $1.11 trillion, though not every line shared in the improvement.

headline: New disclosure rules extend to TPAs administering self-funded health plans
summary: Proposed DOL regulations and the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026 expand advance-disclosure requirements to third-party administrators handling ERISA self-funded group health plans, with new compensation-disclosure duties phasing in for plan years beginning after mid-2026.

headline: Digital tools reshape how third-party administrators handle claims
summary: Third-party administrators across insurance and employee benefits are leaning on automation and data analytics to cut administrative costs and improve transparency, as the global insurance TPA market is projected to grow from roughly $593 billion toward $845 billion by 2031.

headline: Elevance beats Q2 estimates but shares slide on margin worries
summary: Elevance Health topped second-quarter profit expectations and raised full-year guidance to at least $27 adjusted EPS, yet its stock fell more than 10% as investors focused on an 80-basis-point rise in its benefit expense ratio tied to government-program cost trends.

headline: Oregon lifts supervision order over Medicare Advantage insurer ATRIO
summary: Oregon's Division of Financial Regulation ended its supervision of ATRIO Health Plans on July 14, three months after placing the insurer under oversight for a hazardous financial condition tied to over $52 million in 2025 operating losses.

headline: Bank of England regulators unveil plan for new UK captive insurance regime
summary: The PRA and FCA jointly proposed a tailored regulatory framework for captive insurers in the UK, featuring lower capital floors, streamlined governance, faster application turnaround, and reduced reporting burdens, with the new regime targeted to launch in summer 2027 after a consultation closing in October 2026.

headline: Embedded-insurance platform Cover Genius raises $100M, now valued near $2 billion
summary: Cover Genius, a New York-based embedded-protection insurtech, closed a $100 million raise backed by Vista Credit Partners that pushes its valuation to roughly $1.9 billion, with proceeds earmarked for expanding AI-driven personalization and claims tools and funding further acquisitions.

headline: Commercial auto insurers have absorbed more than $10 billion in underwriting losses over two years
summary: Commercial auto liability remains the most stressed P&C line, with carriers continuing to post outsized underwriting losses as claim severity from litigation and jury verdicts keeps outpacing rate increases.

headline: PBM reform wave forces Caremark and peers to overhaul pricing practices
summary: Federal PBM reform actions in 2026, including an FTC settlement requiring Caremark to adopt changes that lower patients' out-of-pocket costs and improve transparency, mark a structural shift toward cost-plus and pass-through pricing models.

headline: Jensten Group deepens its Scottish push with a deal for Glasgow broker Kelvin Smith
summary: UK consolidator Jensten Group agreed to buy Glasgow-based Kelvin Smith Insurance, its third Scottish acquisition of the year, continuing a rapid build-out of its presence north of the border pending regulatory sign-off.

headline: FTC's Caremark settlement aims to lock in $8.5 billion in consumer drug savings
summary: The FTC reached a settlement with Caremark and Zinc Health Services requiring structural changes to formulary design and rebating practices, which the agency estimates could lock in $8.5 billion in consumer savings over a decade.

headline: Fintech Venture Funding Rises 23% in First Half of 2026 Even as Deal Count Falls
summary: Investors poured more capital into fewer, larger fintech deals in H1 2026, with wealth management, financial infrastructure and enterprise automation among the favored categories as venture funding climbed nearly a quarter year-over-year.

headline: NHS England Fast-Tracks £10 Billion AI Rollout to Cut Waiting Times
summary: NHS England is accelerating a £10 billion, three-year AI investment spanning an AI triage tool for 200,000+ patients, ambient voice technology that generates clinical notes in real time, and Microsoft Copilot access for over 500,000 staff.

headline: Canopius taps BCG's Nadine Moore to lead its US specialty insurance business
summary: Lloyd's specialty insurer Canopius Group named Nadine Moore, formerly a managing director and senior partner at Boston Consulting Group, as CEO of its US business effective this September, succeeding Lisa Davis as the carrier scales its US retail and wholesale operations.

headline: MSIG Asia taps QBE veteran Ronak Shah as regional CEO
summary: MSIG Asia named Ronak Shah, previously CEO of QBE's Wholesale Markets Asia, as regional chief executive effective October 1, giving him oversight of operations spanning Southeast Asia, Hong Kong, India and Oceania.

headline: Cover Genius raises $100 million, valuation climbs to $1.9 billion
summary: Embedded-insurance infrastructure provider Cover Genius raised $100 million backed by Vista Credit Partners, funding that will expand its AI-driven personalization, agentic distribution and automated claims capabilities.

headline: Kayna and Willis partner to close subcontractor insurance coverage gaps
summary: Embedded-insurance platform Kayna teamed up with broker Willis to target coverage gaps among subcontractors, aiming to make it easier to verify and bind insurance for gig and trade-based construction workers.

headline: ICICI Prudential Life posts 28% profit jump and record margins in first quarter
summary: ICICI Prudential Life reported first-quarter profit after tax of roughly Rs 386 crore, up nearly 28% year over year, with value of new business climbing almost 25% and margins reaching a record 26.7% on stronger protection sales.

headline: Catastrophe bond issuance hits record $18 billion in first half of 2026
summary: Second-quarter cat bond issuance alone topped $11.3 billion, pushing first-half volume to an all-time high as investor capital continues flooding into insurance-linked securities.

headline: Sun Life's SLC Management names insurance veteran Chris Wei to lead Asia wealth and capital markets push
summary: SLC Management, Sun Life's $309 billion asset management arm, appointed 24-year insurance industry veteran Chris Wei as President of Asia Wealth & Capital Markets, drawing on his prior leadership roles at Great Eastern, AIA and Allstate.

headline: US P&C insurers post best underwriting result in a decade
summary: Private US property/casualty insurers logged a $15.8 billion first-quarter 2026 underwriting gain, reversing a year-earlier loss, building on 2025's best combined ratio in ten years and $1.11 trillion in direct premiums written.

headline: NFP acquires Cleveland retirement and benefits advisory firm Total Benefits Advisors
summary: Aon-owned broker NFP announced the acquisition of Total Benefits Advisors, a Cleveland, Ohio firm spanning retirement services, employee benefits and wealth management for business owners and high-net-worth clients.

headline: Fiduciary Services Group acquires New Jersey retirement plan TPA RetireWell Administrators
summary: The deal, FSG's third TPA acquisition of 2026, adds a New Jersey third-party administrator serving more than 425 retirement plans to the firm's DWC recordkeeping and administration business.

headline: EZLynx partners with First Connect to extend all-in-one agency management system to member agents
summary: The partnership gives First Connect's network of independent agents discounted access to EZLynx's agency management platform, bundling automation and AI across policy management, accounting and marketing.

headline: Elevance Health raises full-year guidance after medical costs come in below expectations
summary: Elevance posted adjusted second-quarter EPS of $7.45, well above Wall Street estimates, and lifted its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $27.00 while targeting a return to 12% earnings growth in 2027.

headline: Senators press UnitedHealthcare, Humana and CVS Health over AI-driven prior authorization denials
summary: Sens. Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley sent letters demanding records on how each insurer's Medicare Advantage plans use algorithms in post-acute care coverage decisions, giving the companies until July 28 to respond.

headline: DC recordkeeping assets keep concentrating even as $600 billion in annual outflows cap growth
summary: Morningstar data shows defined contribution recordkeeping assets have jumped since 2020 and collective investment trusts keep gaining share, but roughly $600 billion a year in outflows to rollovers and withdrawals is capping overall system growth.

headline: ACA marketplace insurers push through steepest rate hikes in years as subsidy cliff looms
summary: Insurers are filing average marketplace premium increases near 26% for the coming plan year, the sharpest jump since 2018, largely because carriers are pricing in the scheduled expiration of enhanced federal premium tax credits and anticipate healthier members exiting the risk pool.

headline: Former Humana and CVS chief executives lend their names to an AI health insurance upstart
summary: Ex-CEOs of Humana and CVS Health have signed on as advisors to Optura, an AI-focused healthcare startup, with UnitedHealth Group also joining the advisory effort, underscoring how veteran payer leadership is migrating toward AI-native ventures.

headline: UK and EU regulators sharpen valuation and NAV-reporting expectations for private-market funds
summary: A July 2026 regulatory update highlights growing scrutiny of valuation processes for private-market exposures in retail-oriented investment products, as investor demand for timelier NAV reporting increases across UK and EU asset managers.

headline: Embedded-insurance platform Cover Genius lands $100M credit round, nears $2B valuation
summary: Cover Genius secured a $100 million growth investment from Vista Credit Partners at a $1.9 billion valuation, its first credit-structured raise, to expand AI capabilities and pursue acquisitions across its point-of-sale insurance network.

headline: HCA Healthcare trims 2026 profit guidance as uninsured patient volumes rise
summary: HCA lowered its full-year net income forecast by roughly $1 billion, blaming the fallout from ACA marketplace disruption and softer surgical volumes; the news dragged down shares across other for-profit hospital operators too.

headline: US commercial P&C rate growth cools to softest pace since 2017
summary: Alera Group's midyear analysis found commercial property/casualty premium growth flattened to roughly 0.2% in H1 2026 as insurer competition intensifies, marking the mildest pricing environment in nearly a decade even as some catastrophe-exposed lines stay firm.

headline: Feathery raises $30M Series A to expand AI decisioning into insurance and wealth management
summary: Feathery closed a $30 million Series A backed by Portage Ventures, Index Ventures, Allstate Strategic Ventures and Erie Strategic Ventures, among others, to grow its AI-powered workflow and decisioning platform across financial services including insurance and wealth management.

headline: Great Wealth Transfer and 'Peak 65' reshape 2026 life and annuity demand
summary: Industry analysis frames the generational handoff of wealth from boomers to millennials and Gen Z, alongside record numbers of Americans turning 65, as the defining force pushing lifetime-income products to the center of retirement planning conversations.

headline: BlackRock posts record margin and $192 billion of net inflows in Q2
summary: BlackRock's second-quarter results beat Wall Street estimates, with assets under management reaching $15.3 trillion and quarterly net inflows nearly tripling from a year earlier, pushing operating margin to a five-year high.

headline: Hanover Insurance names COO Richard Lavey as CEO-elect
summary: The Hanover Insurance Group disclosed that Chief Operating Officer Richard W. Lavey will become CEO-elect and succeed President and CEO John C. Roche, who plans to retire at the end of 2026.

headline: Allstate hires former CoStar finance chief as new CFO
summary: Allstate named a new chief financial officer with more than 25 years of capital-markets and leadership experience, most recently as CFO of commercial real estate data firm CoStar Group.

headline: Sanford Health and Marshfield Clinic finalize $10 billion merger
summary: Sanford Health completed its combination with Marshfield Clinic Health System less than six months after announcing the deal, forming a 56-hospital nonprofit system and welcoming 13,000 new employees, with Sanford committing $500 million to Marshfield facilities over five years.

headline: Elevance Health Shares Tumble Despite Earnings Beat as Margins Shrink
summary: Elevance topped quarterly profit and revenue estimates and raised its full-year guidance, yet its stock sold off as investors focused on shrinking operating margins in its core health-benefits and Medicaid business. The mixed reaction dragged down shares of peer managed-care insurers as well.

headline: India's newer specialised investment fund category posts sharp monthly asset growth
summary: Assets in India's Specialised Investment Fund category climbed 29% in June 2026 to about Rs 17,858 crore according to a ValueMetrics report, with hybrid long-short strategies making up nearly three-quarters of the category's total assets.

headline: Vanguard and Fidelity push ahead with target-date fund glide-path overhauls as TDF assets near $5 trillion
summary: Both fund giants are mid-way through reallocating target-date series toward higher equity exposure in early-dated vintages, changes Morningstar says continue to reshape the nearly $5 trillion target-date fund category that anchors most workplace retirement defaults.

headline: CMS finalizes 2027 Medicare Advantage rates with payments up nearly 5% for insurers
summary: The Trump administration backed off elements of its original Medicare Advantage rate proposal, finalizing 2027 payment rates that raise average per-enrollee payments to private insurers by close to 5%, roughly double the initially proposed increase.

headline: UK's new Pension Schemes Act rewrites the rules for workplace DC saving
summary: The Pension Schemes Act 2026 has become law, creating a trustee duty to offer default retirement-income solutions for defined-contribution savers and setting new scale requirements for multi-employer default arrangements from 2030.

headline: Retirement-plan TPA consolidation continues as Fiduciary Services Group buys Pension Investors Corp
summary: The parent of DWC – The 401(k) Experts is absorbing a Florida-based administrator overseeing about 900 retirement plans, folding the business into its existing TPA operations.

headline: IRDAI's one-hour cashless claim mandate shows uneven compliance across insurers
summary: India's insurance regulator's rule requiring insurers to clear cashless pre-authorization within an hour is now being met in about 87% of cases, per 2026 regulatory data, with some insurers still lagging on turnaround times.

headline: Private capital keeps building stakes in life insurers and annuity platforms
summary: Recent deals such as Avocet Partners' purchase of EMC Life and Aquarian Holdings' acquisition of Brighthouse Financial show private capital sponsors' continued appetite to acquire or partner with life and annuity platforms as the convergence between life insurance and private capital deepens.

headline: Ambient AI documentation tools cut hours of charting time at major health systems
summary: Intermountain Health cut time spent on visit notes by 27% using Microsoft's Dragon Copilot, while Cooper University Healthcare and a nursing team at Mercy in Missouri each reported saving more than an hour of documentation time per shift.

headline: US wildfire activity running well above historical average in 2026
summary: More than 42000 fires had burned upward of 4.5 million acres across the US by July 2026, about 130% of the ten-year average, as wildfire's share of insured catastrophe losses keeps climbing.

headline: Target-Date Fund Assets Swell to $4.8 Trillion as Collective Trusts Overtake Mutual Funds
summary: Morningstar's 2026 target-date landscape report shows industry assets grew more than 20% last year to $4.8 trillion, with the top five providers controlling about 80% of the market and collective investment trusts now the leading vehicle ahead of mutual funds.

headline: Private-Equity-Backed Reinsurers Are Absorbing a Growing Slice of Life and Annuity Risk
summary: S&P Global Market Intelligence finds affiliated, PE-owned reinsurers are taking on an increasing share of ceded life and annuity liabilities, as alternative asset managers keep pursuing stable long-duration liabilities to feed their investment platforms.

headline: Global insurtech funding hits four-year high of $2.44 billion in Q2 2026 as AI captures 99% of capital
summary: Gallagher Re's latest report found AI-focused insurtechs took in $2.42 billion across 95 deals in the quarter, with every round above $5 million going to an AI company and mega-rounds of $100 million-plus making up over two-thirds of the total.

headline: Target-date fund assets near $5 trillion as low-cost trusts overtake mutual funds
summary: Target-date strategy assets grew 20.3% in 2025 to $4.8 trillion, with collective investment trusts now holding the majority share as plan sponsors chase lower fees, even as scrutiny grows over whether traditional glide paths manage risk adequately.

headline: Industry body warns Asia's private health insurers face a sustainability crisis within years
summary: GAIP cautioned that runaway medical cost inflation — projected as high as 16.9% in Singapore and topping 12.5% regionally — could push Asia-Pacific private health insurance into a full-blown crisis within two to three years absent reform.

headline: Empower to acquire Milliman's retirement administration business for $340 million
summary: Empower agreed to acquire Milliman's retirement plan administration unit for $340 million, a deal expected to close in the second half of 2026 and add roughly 400 defined-benefit plans and about 790,000 plan participants to Empower's recordkeeping platform.

headline: DOL maps out 2026 retirement rulemaking, from e-delivery rules to benchmarking guidance
summary: The Department of Labor's latest regulatory agenda includes a proposed SECURE 2.0 rule on paper benefit statements and e-disclosure starting with the 2026 plan year, plus a target of October 2026 for guidance letting blended-asset investments be benchmarked against a mix of market indices.

headline: CVC completes takeover of US credit manager Marathon Asset Management
summary: European private equity firm CVC Capital Partners closed its roughly $1.2-1.6 billion acquisition of Marathon Asset Management, rebranding the $24 billion credit specialist as CVC Marathon with a goal of growing the combined credit platform toward EUR200 billion in fee-paying assets by 2028.

headline: Global catastrophe losses ran well below trend in first half of 2026, Swiss Re says
summary: Swiss Re Institute estimated global insured natural catastrophe losses at about $42 billion for H1 2026, the lowest first-half total since 2020 and well under the long-term trend, even as underlying exposure keeps rising.

headline: AI now handles most prior authorization decisions, but debate over fairness grows
summary: Roughly 84% of US health insurers are using AI for prior authorization and claims tasks in 2026, and industry pledges have cut request volumes by about 11%, even as critics question whether automation is speeding approvals or just automating denials.

headline: Apollo executive points to Asia's aging population as a major investment opportunity
summary: Apollo Global Management's Eiji Ueda argued that shifting demographics and rising retirement needs across Asia are opening a substantial new opportunity for asset managers to deploy capital into the region's retirement and income markets.

headline: Asset and wealth management deal volume rises 22% as buyers stay active despite headwinds
summary: PwC's midyear 2026 outlook found first-quarter asset and wealth management deal volume climbed 22% versus the prior quarter, signaling continued buyer conviction in strategic M&A despite a choppier macro backdrop.

headline: Antares Global Launches New Scorpius MGA Platform
summary: Antares Global rolled out Scorpius, a new managing general agent platform, as part of continued investment by London market players in dedicated MGA technology infrastructure.

headline: APAC insurtech investment has roughly halved since 2022 as capital turns cautious
summary: Insurtech funding across Asia-Pacific fell from about $9.1 billion to $4.1 billion between 2022 and 2025, reflecting investors' broader retreat from early-stage insurance technology bets in the region.

headline: Australian Insurer GMHBA Recruits Superannuation Chief Jarrod Coysh as Next CEO
summary: Not-for-profit health insurer GMHBA named REI Super chief executive Jarrod Coysh as its incoming CEO, succeeding David Greig, in a cross-sector hire the board says reflects pressure on the insurer's value proposition from rising out-of-pocket costs.

headline: AI-native carrier Corgi raises $108 million and wins regulatory approval to underwrite startups
summary: Corgi secured $108 million in funding along with regulatory authority to operate as a full-stack, AI-native insurance carrier focused on startup companies, with plans to expand coverage options and invest further in underwriting and claims automation.

headline: BlackRock's assets under management climb to $15.3 trillion in the second quarter
summary: BlackRock reported AUM of $15.3 trillion for Q2 2026, with net inflows of $192 billion in the quarter and $321 billion for the first half, driven by ETFs, private markets and systematic equity strategies.

headline: Insurtech funding accelerates in 2026 as AI-focused deals dominate
summary: Insurtech funding accelerated sharply in 2026, with digital insurance brokers capturing roughly three-quarters of year-to-date funding; CB Insights data shows Q1 2026 alone saw about $1.63 billion raised, with 95% of that flowing to AI-focused companies.

headline: DOL grants temporary relief as plan sponsors scramble to comply with new paper statement rule
summary: The Department of Labor issued Field Assistance Bulletin 2026-02 giving retirement plan administrators temporary enforcement relief while they build compliance processes for the revived requirement to mail at least one paper benefit statement per year.

headline: KKR joins Amwins-led consortium in A$7.7 billion approach for Australian broker Steadfast
summary: Global investment firm KKR joined Amwins Group and Dragoneer Investment in a consortium proposal to acquire Australian insurance broker network Steadfast for roughly A$7.7 billion (US$5.33 billion).

headline: CMS signals plan to overhaul how it pays for clinical software and AI
summary: CMS indicated in proposed 2027 hospital-outpatient and physician-fee rules that it intends to build a more consistent payment structure for clinical software and AI tools tied to their measured impact on patient outcomes.

headline: Mayo Clinic now runs over 150 AI models across its hospital system
summary: Mayo Clinic has deployed more than 150 AI models system-wide, including "Record Time," a tool that generates chronological patient summaries and saves physicians five to thirty minutes of prep per visit.

headline: UnitedHealth beats Q2 2026 estimates, raises full-year profit guidance
summary: UnitedHealth reported second-quarter revenue of $112 billion and adjusted earnings of $6.38 per share, raising full-year adjusted guidance to $19.50-$20.00 per share as its medical cost ratio improved from the prior year.

headline: Mayo Clinic runs roughly 150 AI models in production, including a new tool to speed chart review
summary: Mayo Clinic clinicians are using a new AI tool that generates chronological patient summaries and makes searching medical records faster, part of a broader deployment of around 150 AI models across the hospital.

headline: American Growth Insurance debuts as AI-enabled brokerage platform with roughly $70 million in backing
summary: American Growth Insurance launched as an AI-enabled specialty brokerage growth platform with nearly $70 million in committed equity funding from Rockbridge Growth Equity and venture studio Atomic.

headline: Global commercial insurance rates turn negative for the first time in seven years
summary: Ahead of Q2 earnings, analysts point to the Marsh Global Insurance Market Index falling to roughly -4%, with the steepest declines in commercial property, workers' comp, cyber and D&O, even as US casualty and commercial auto keep hardening on social inflation and nuclear verdicts.

headline: NYU Langone builds AI tool to flag patients needing care after discharge
summary: NYU Langone embedded a discharge-prediction tool directly into its Epic EHR system to flag internal-medicine patients likely to need continued care after leaving the hospital, with plans to expand it using emergency-department and therapy notes.

headline: American Growth Insurance launches with $70 million to build AI-native brokerage platform
summary: Atlanta-based American Growth Insurance debuted as an AI-enabled specialty brokerage growth platform backed by Rockbridge Growth Equity and Atomic, saying its AI-first operating model lifted average partner-agency profitability by more than 50%.

headline: Foxen Embeds Discounted Pet Insurance Into Rental Property Platform
summary: PropTech firm Foxen has partnered with Healthy Paws to build pet insurance offers directly into its PetClear renter platform, giving qualifying tenants a discount and a simplified path to purchase coverage.

headline: CMS moves to overhaul how Medicare reimburses clinical AI and remote monitoring
summary: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services is proposing significant changes to payment models for clinical AI tools and remote patient monitoring, a shift that could reshape how health systems justify and scale AI investments going forward.

headline: Wealth Enhancement expands Houston footprint with $299 million Trippon acquisition
summary: Wealth Enhancement closed its purchase of Trippon Wealth Management Group and its affiliated CPA practice, adding roughly $299 million in client assets and pushing the RIA aggregator past $158 billion in total client assets.

headline: US wealthtech deal count jumps 27% in Q2 2026 even as total funding declines
summary: US wealthtech recorded 116 deals in the second quarter of 2026, up 27% year-over-year, even though total funding fell 41% to $557.8 million as investors favored more, smaller rounds over mega-deals.

headline: Excess and surplus lines property rate softening accelerates as casualty increases slow
summary: CRC Group's REDY report shows property rate softening picking up pace in the excess and surplus market even as the rate of casualty rate increases begins to decelerate, reflecting the broader bifurcation in the US commercial market.

headline: UnitedHealth Group's Q2 profit hits $5.4 billion as medical costs ease
summary: UnitedHealth Group reported second-quarter net income of $5.48 billion and raised its 2026 earnings forecast after its medical care ratio fell to 86.7% from 89.4% a year earlier, aided by benefit redesign and exits from unprofitable ACA and Medicare Advantage markets.

headline: Insurers keep piling into private credit even as market volatility raises eyebrows
summary: Insurers globally continue to expand private credit holdings in pursuit of higher yields and diversification, with the median allocation across insurer types now around 9%, up sharply from 2018, and roughly six in ten insurers planning further increases over the next two years.

headline: Wealth Enhancement grows its Houston presence with a tax-focused practice acquisition
summary: RIA aggregator Wealth Enhancement acquired Trippon, a roughly $299 million integrated tax-and-wealth planning practice, deepening its Houston footprint as part of its ongoing acquisition strategy centered on combined financial and tax services.

headline: Florida regulators weigh stricter exam and disclosure requirements for property insurers
summary: Florida's insurance department scheduled a hearing on proposed rule changes that would tighten market conduct examinations and reporting obligations for property insurers operating in the state.

headline: Commercial insurance rates keep softening across most lines in second quarter
summary: The latest Ivans Index shows renewal rates declining further in Q2 2026 for property, general liability and auto lines, while workers' comp and casualty diverge, signaling a broadening soft market for US commercial insurers.

headline: Insurance-infrastructure startup Yuzu Health lands $35 million Series A
summary: Yuzu Health, which pivoted from building its own health plan to modernizing the back-end systems insurers use to administer coverage, closed a $35 million round led by General Catalyst and Chemistry with backing from Anthropic's venture arm.

headline: Invesco closes takeover of Morgan Stanley's retail asset management arm
summary: Invesco completed its previously announced purchase of Morgan Stanley's retail asset management business, including the Van Kampen lineup, as consolidation among traditional asset managers continues to accelerate.

headline: InsuranceDekho lines up ~$1B IPO, targets September DRHP filing
summary: India's InsuranceDekho is preparing to file its draft IPO prospectus with SEBI by the end of September, reportedly seeking a valuation near ₹9,500 crore as it heads toward a public listing before March 2027.

headline: UnitedHealth beats Q2, hikes 2026 profit outlook as costs ease
summary: UnitedHealth posted a large Q2 2026 earnings beat with a lower medical care ratio and raised full-year guidance, even while flagging expected member losses in ACA and Medicare Advantage plans due to affordability pressure.

headline: England to screen every newborn for spinal muscular atrophy
summary: The UK government confirmed on July 16 that newborn screening for spinal muscular atrophy will roll out nationwide across England, paired with a national evaluation program to track outcomes.

headline: Intermountain Health cuts charting time 27% after system-wide Dragon Copilot rollout
summary: Intermountain Health found that clinicians using Microsoft's Dragon Copilot ambient AI in 10 or more encounters saw a 27% reduction in time spent on notes per appointment, after a phased rollout that trained more than 1,400 staff with Accenture over 13 weeks.

headline: PremFina secures £400 million debt facility from Lloyds as loan book triples
summary: UK insurance premium-finance provider PremFina secured a new £400 million senior debt facility from Lloyds, complementing an existing £100 million junior facility, after its loan book grew more than 300% over 18 months.

headline: Yvette Cooper takes over as UK Health and Social Care Secretary
summary: Cooper was appointed the UK's new Secretary of State for Health and Social Care and said she would prioritize maternity services and social care reform alongside ongoing NHS leadership changes.

headline: Hanover Insurance sets up leadership handover as longtime CEO Roche plans exit
summary: The Hanover Insurance Group said President and CEO John Roche will retire at the end of 2026 after roughly a decade in the role, with Chief Operating Officer Richard Lavey named CEO-elect to take over.

headline: Clinical AI startup Bunkerhill Health raises $55 million to expand agentic AI tools inside hospitals
summary: Bunkerhill Health closed a Series B led by Khosla Ventures, with Sequoia, Felicis, Optum Ventures and Y Combinator participating, bringing total funding to $55 million to scale its Carebricks platform that lets health systems build AI agents for clinical, operational and administrative tasks; the platform is already live at Cleveland Clinic, UTMB and Intermountain Health.

headline: Indian life insurers push AI deeper into underwriting and claims workflows
summary: ICICI Prudential Life and HDFC Life are moving artificial intelligence from pilot projects into everyday underwriting, claims processing, fraud detection and servicing, part of a broader industry shift toward AI-driven efficiency across the policy lifecycle.

headline: Retirement giant Voya draws renewed takeover interest
summary: Voya Financial, which manages roughly $350 billion in retirement assets, is reportedly fielding ongoing acquisition interest from suitors including Principal Financial, underscoring continued consolidation appetite in the defined-contribution recordkeeping business.

headline: UnitedHealth stock jumps after insurer tops estimates and lifts its 2026 profit forecast
summary: UnitedHealth shares surged roughly 10% after the company beat quarterly expectations and raised its full-year earnings outlook, with executives citing improving medical-cost trends.

headline: UnitedHealth swings back with $112 billion Q2, raises 2026 profit outlook
summary: UnitedHealth Group's Q2 2026 revenue reached $112 billion with adjusted EPS of $6.38, and the insurer raised full-year adjusted earnings guidance to $19.50-$20 per share as its medical cost ratio improved to 86.7%.

headline: UnitedHealth Group Posts Big Earnings Beat, Raises 2026 Profit Outlook
summary: UnitedHealth Group reported second-quarter 2026 results well ahead of analyst expectations, with operating earnings climbing to $8 billion and a materially improved medical-cost ratio, prompting the insurer to raise its full-year adjusted earnings guidance as its margin-recovery strategy takes hold.

headline: SEC Proposes Rule to Expand Electronic Delivery of Investor Disclosures
summary: The SEC proposed Regulation E-Delivery in July 2026, which would broaden the ability of investment advisers, broker-dealers and issuers to satisfy federal disclosure requirements through electronic delivery rather than paper mailings.

headline: UnitedHealth tops Q2 estimates and raises full-year guidance on cost control
summary: UnitedHealth posted a $5.5 billion second-quarter profit and again raised its 2026 earnings outlook, even as executives cautioned that easing commercial medical cost trends reflect active cost management rather than a durable trend reversal.

headline: Bipartisan House bill would require physician sign-off on AI-driven Medicare Advantage denials
summary: Representatives Greg Murphy and Herb Conaway introduced legislation requiring a qualified physician to review and approve any AI-assisted Medicare Advantage coverage denial, with the plan's medical director attesting the decision reflected independent medical judgment.

headline: Australian underwriting agency Blue Zebra renews multi-year QBE motor capacity deal
summary: Blue Zebra, an Australian MGA, extended its multi-year capacity agreement with QBE covering personal and commercial motor lines, alongside a strengthened specialist underwriting and claims team.

headline: One Inc and CalcFocus team up to modernize life insurance premium payments
summary: Payment platform One Inc partnered with policy administration provider CalcFocus to integrate One Inc's PremiumPay into life insurers' systems, giving policyholders more digital payment options including Apple Pay, Google Pay and Venmo.

headline: SME lender Forward Financing lands $525 million funding package
summary: Forward Financing secured $525 million to expand small-business lending capacity, part of a broader week of heavy fintech fundraising that also touched insurance- and wealth-adjacent platforms.

headline: Hospital operating margins slip to 2.6% in July as costs keep outpacing revenue
summary: National hospital operating margins fell to 2.6% on average in July, down from 3.4% in June, with rising workforce, supply and drug costs continuing to squeeze profitability even as bad debt and charity care climb.

headline: Indexed annuity trade group pushes back on proposed illustration rule changes
summary: The Indexed Annuity Leadership Council submitted comments to the NAIC's Life Insurance and Annuities Illustrations working group opposing parts of a proposed overhaul of Model #245, the annuity disclosure regulation, ahead of further working-group review.

headline: Insurers' Q2 books get a lift as investment income outruns catastrophe losses
summary: Travelers posted 14% growth in net investment income to roughly $1.07 billion pre-tax in Q2 2026 as a stronger fixed-income portfolio and lighter storm losses drove net income to $2.21 billion, part of a broader pattern of insurers benefiting from elevated yields this earnings season.

headline: Fintech funding hits $1.9bn for the week as insurtech holds a steady share of deals
summary: Weekly fintech investment tracking showed roughly $1.9 billion raised across the sector, with wealthtech, financial-infrastructure and blockchain firms leading deal counts while insurtech companies secured a handful of the week's rounds.

headline: Mid-July hailstorms across France and Germany push European insured losses toward a billion euros
summary: A sequence of severe convective storms across Europe from July 10-17 drove hail, wind and flash-flood damage concentrated in France and Germany, with Aon estimating aggregate losses of at least hundreds of millions of euros and potential to reach a billion-euro industry event.

headline: Higher yields lift insurer investment income across Q2 earnings season
summary: Travelers reported a 14% jump in net investment income to $1.07 billion in the second quarter as its fixed-income portfolio benefited from higher yields and a larger asset base, a pattern echoed across other P&C carriers' Q2 results.

headline: Catastrophe reinsurance prices post steepest annual drop in 25 years
summary: Global property-catastrophe reinsurance rates fell roughly 16% year-on-year at the June/July 2026 renewals, the sharpest annual decline in a quarter-century, as record reinsurance capital and a fifth consecutive quarter of below-average catastrophe losses gave cedents more negotiating leverage.

headline: Altruist launches AI planning agent 'Hazel' as AI-native wealth manager Arca raises $64 million
summary: Custodial platform Altruist rolled out an AI-driven financial planning agent for advisors, the same week AI-native wealth manager Arca closed a $64 million funding round, underscoring how fast agentic AI is moving into core advisor workflows.

headline: Insurers keep piling into private debt despite tighter spreads
summary: AllianceBernstein's latest insurance-investor commentary argues that private debt remains attractive for insurers matching long-duration liabilities, even as compressed illiquidity premiums make manager selection and structuring more important than ever.

headline: Majority of insurers plan to deepen private credit bets over the next two years
summary: A survey found 57% of insurers expect to raise private credit allocations over the next 12-24 months, outpacing appetite for investment-grade public fixed income, as US life insurers' private credit and illiquid holdings climb toward $807 billion.

headline: London Broker Howden Explores Major Capital Raise Ahead of Possible IPO
summary: Howden Group is reportedly pursuing a substantial capital raise as it positions itself for a potential future public listing, continuing the London-based broker's aggressive global expansion strategy.

headline: UnitedHealth's medical cost ratio holds at 86.7% in Q2 on pricing discipline
summary: UnitedHealth Group reported an 86.7% medical cost ratio for the second quarter of 2026, aided by $860 million in favorable prior-period reserve development, as the insurer pointed to improved cost and pricing discipline.

headline: Malibu Life buys TruSpire to build a US retail annuity origination arm
summary: Malibu Life Holdings acquired TruSpire as part of a push to move beyond reinsurance and establish a direct annuity origination platform in the US market.

headline: Manipal Hospitals' Rs 6,300-crore Sahyadri buyout reshapes Indian care
summary: Manipal Hospitals is acquiring Sahyadri Hospitals in a roughly Rs 6,300 crore deal that adds 11 hospitals across Maharashtra, marking one of the largest consolidation moves yet in India's hospital sector.

headline: Sanctuary Wealth adds $5.9 billion in new assets in H1 2026, lifting total client assets to $65.7 billion
summary: Hybrid RIA platform Sanctuary Wealth grew total client assets to $65.7 billion, more than doubling since 2023, as advisor teams continued seeking flexible affiliation models away from wirehouses.

headline: Accelerated Wealth Partners makes its first investment, backing a $1.6 billion Houston RIA
summary: Newly formed RIA consolidator Accelerated Wealth Partners announced its debut deal, taking a stake in a Houston-based registered investment advisor overseeing roughly $1.6 billion in client assets.

headline: Advisor360 debuts an AI-native operating system for wealth advisors
summary: Advisor360 launched a new AI-native platform aimed at consolidating advisor workflows, part of a broader wealthtech push to embed generative AI directly into planning and portfolio tools.

headline: Orion180 lifts reinsurance coverage 36% to $1.15 billion ahead of hurricane season
summary: The Florida-based insurer expanded its 2026 reinsurance tower and broadened the number of catastrophic events covered as it prepares for the Atlantic hurricane season.

headline: Vantage Group taps former Arch Capital chief as it plots CEO succession
summary: Vantage named ex-Arch Capital CEO Marc Grandisson as executive chairman effective immediately, with David Gansberg set to become CEO once his non-compete obligations lapse in 2027.

headline: US Regulators Miss Their Own Deadline to Finalize Stablecoin Rules Under the GENIUS Act
summary: The one-year statutory deadline for federal agencies to complete detailed rules implementing the GENIUS Act, the US stablecoin framework, passed without finished regulations, even though the OCC, FDIC, Treasury and other regulators had issued proposed rules in a last-minute push.

headline: Malibu Life installs ex-Prudential retirement chief as new CEO
summary: Malibu Life named Todd Shriber, formerly Prudential Financial's COO for global retirement and insurance, as CEO effective July 20, 2026, succeeding Gary Dombowsky as the firm expands into annuities and retirement distribution.

headline: Harrison Street folds its European arm into RoundShield, creating a rebranded platform
summary: Harrison Street Asset Management announced it is integrating its European investment operations into RoundShield Partners, with the combined business rebranding as HSAM Europe, a year after Harrison Street first took a majority stake in RoundShield.

headline: UK cabinet reshuffle installs Yvette Cooper as Health Secretary
summary: Cooper moved from the Foreign Office to take charge of health and social care policy, with maternity-care improvements and social-care reform cited as immediate priorities for the NHS.

headline: Fidelity follows Vanguard and BlackRock in wiring annuities into 401(k) target-date funds
summary: Fidelity plans to launch a 'Freedom Lifetime' collective investment trust suite in early 2027 that embeds guaranteed lifetime income from Nationwide and New York Life into target-date funds, joining Vanguard-TIAA and BlackRock's LifePath Paycheck in mainstreaming in-plan annuities.

headline: PE-backed emergency medicine groups team up on Dignity Health contracts
summary: Emergency Care Partners, backed by Varsity Healthcare Partners, MidOcean Partners and Regal Healthcare Capital, struck a partnership with Phoenix-based Empower Emergency Physicians to staff Dignity Health's St. Joseph's hospitals.

headline: IRDAI clears another general insurance licence as 100% FDI draws fresh foreign interest
summary: India's insurance regulator approved a further general insurance licence, the second since the government raised the foreign direct investment ceiling to 100%, as overseas capital continues to target the sector.

headline: Commercial buyers see property and cyber relief while casualty costs keep climbing
summary: Alliant Insurance Services' mid-year report finds U.S. commercial insurance buyers getting rate relief in property and cyber lines, with property rates down high single digits to more than 20% in places, while casualty and transportation risks remain pressured by litigation costs and large verdicts.

headline: Odyssey Group's Carl Overy adds president and CEO role at Hudson Insurance Group
summary: Carl Overy, chief executive of Odyssey Group, has taken on the additional role of president and CEO of Hudson Insurance Group, expanding his leadership responsibilities across the specialty insurer's operations.

headline: American Growth Insurance launches AI-enabled brokerage growth platform with ~$70M backing
summary: American Growth Insurance launched an AI-enabled specialty brokerage growth platform backed by nearly $70 million in committed equity from Rockbridge Growth Equity and venture studio Atomic, after piloting the AI-first operating model with agencies that saw profitability gains of more than 50%.

headline: DC plan sponsors show rising appetite for alternative investments but need lineup guidance
summary: A NAPA-Net report finds 44% of defined contribution plan sponsors are interested in adding alternative investments to 401(k) lineups, with large and mega plans showing the strongest enthusiasm at 62% and 50% respectively.

headline: NHS pushes new sepsis-prevention and quality strategy
summary: NHS England outlined new measures aimed at preventing thousands of sepsis deaths by 2035 as part of a broader Quality Strategy for NHS-funded care, alongside record cancer-check volumes reaching 3.4 million patients in a year.

headline: Marsh's Q2 revenue climbs as it leans further into producers and AI
summary: Business Insurance's weekly roundup highlights Marsh investing further in both frontline producers and AI tooling as a driver of its second-quarter revenue growth, alongside a wave of other broker technology moves.

headline: Court challenge threatens to unwind parts of CMS's 2027 Medicare Advantage star-ratings overhaul
summary: A legal win by smaller carrier Clover Health against elements of CMS's revised Medicare Advantage star-ratings methodology could force regulators to revisit a rule that was expected to steer billions more in quality bonus payments to insurers.

headline: State-run Central Bank of India to enter wealth management and card business for fee income
summary: Central Bank of India's CEO said the state-owned lender has board approval to launch wealth management and re-enter the credit-card business in the second half of the fiscal year as it seeks to boost non-interest income.

headline: Apollo Hospitals Set to Outpace Rivals as India's Hospital Chains Post Strong Quarter
summary: Analysts at Jefferies expect India's major hospital operators, including Apollo Hospitals, Max Healthcare, Fortis, and Global Health, to post double-digit revenue growth this quarter on strong patient volumes. Apollo is forecast to lead the group even as new-facility expansion costs weigh on sector margins.

headline: RIA dealmaking hits record pace in first half of 2026, fueled by private equity
summary: Wealth management M&A surged in the first half of 2026, with 225 deals involving RIAs holding at least $100 million in assets announced through June, up 39% from a year earlier, as private-equity-backed firms accounted for the vast majority of strategic buyers.

headline: Malibu Life recruits a Prudential retirement executive as its new chief executive
summary: London-listed reinsurer Malibu Life Holdings named Todd Shriber, formerly head of strategy for Prudential Financial's global retirement and insurance businesses, as CEO effective July 20, as the firm expands into US direct annuity origination following its TruSpire acquisition.

headline: Pooled Employer Plan adoption jumps 45% as recordkeepers make PEPs a strategic priority
summary: The 2026 PLANSPONSOR/Cerulli recordkeeping survey found 10,797 employers have now adopted PEPs for their 401(k) or 403(b) participants, up from 7,454 a year earlier, with most recordkeepers calling PEPs a major or moderate strategic priority.

headline: Fidelity, Vanguard and BlackRock push annuities into target-date 401(k) funds
summary: Major asset managers are building annuity-linked options into target-date funds, with Fidelity's planned Freedom Lifetime fund set to let retirees convert savings into guaranteed lifetime income from insurers starting in 2027.

headline: Wealth management panel says AI agents are the next major wave of advisor software
summary: Industry panelists at a WealthManagement.com event argued that 2026 will be remembered as the year AI agents move beyond meeting note-taking into broader advisory workflows, even as most advisors are still just testing the tools.

headline: PBGC's swelling $62 billion surplus stokes a push to cut pension premiums
summary: A widening surplus at the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation is fueling pressure from plan sponsors and advocacy groups to reform single-employer premium levels, which critics say no longer match the agency's shrinking risk exposure.

headline: Plan sponsors face a year-end deadline to true up SECURE 2.0 paperwork
summary: Many employers have operationally adopted SECURE 2.0 provisions through recordkeepers and payroll providers without formally amending plan documents, and the compliance grace period requiring documents to match practice closes December 31, 2026.

headline: Chubb installs new dual leadership atop its Tempest Re reinsurance arm
summary: Chubb named James Wixtead executive chairman and promoted Michael O'Donnell to president of Chubb Tempest Re effective August 1, with O'Donnell assuming day-to-day operating responsibility for the global reinsurance business.

headline: US insurance agency M&A volume falls to a seven-year low
summary: North American insurance agency acquisitions dropped to 292 deals in the first half of 2026, down 15% year over year, with P&C agencies accounting for 68% of transactions as buyers pulled back.

headline: RIA M&A on pace for busiest year yet as market nears $4 trillion
summary: Cerulli Associates reports RIA consolidation is driving deal activity toward a record pace in 2026 as the independent advisory market approaches $4 trillion in assets.

headline: Chubb names James Wixtead executive chairman of Chubb Tempest Re
summary: Chubb announced leadership changes at its global reinsurance arm, Chubb Tempest Re, naming James Wixtead executive chairman as part of a broader round of executive moves across Chubb, Marsh and Aon.

headline: New CAA and DOL rules expand disclosure duties for TPAs and PBMs
summary: The Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026 and a proposed DOL rule extend compensation-disclosure requirements to third-party administrators, PBMs and stop-loss insurers servicing self-funded health plans, with plan sponsors on the hook if service providers fail to comply.

headline: Aviva writes another large UK pension risk-transfer deal, this time for Aston Martin's scheme
summary: Aviva completed a roughly £180 million bulk purchase annuity buy-in covering around 540 pensioners and 1,050 deferred members of the Aston Martin Lagonda Pension Scheme, continuing its run of UK defined-benefit de-risking transactions.

headline: Consolidation continues to reshape the third-party administrator sector
summary: Employee Benefit News reports private equity and larger benefits players are increasingly acquiring third-party administrators as the TPA market consolidates around scale and technology investment.

headline: State regulators widen their multi-state trial of an AI oversight tool for insurers
summary: The NAIC's pilot of its AI Systems Evaluation Tool, which tests how regulators can assess insurers' AI governance and third-party model risk, has grown to 12 participating states after California joined. The program runs through September 2026 and is expected to inform a broader adoption decision at the NAIC's fall national meeting.

headline: Hospital M&A activity accelerates through 2026 as health systems resume dealmaking
summary: Health systems that paused deals in 2025 amid policy uncertainty have resumed mergers, with 40 hospital transactions announced in the first half of 2026, including Community Health Systems' planned sale of its three-hospital Commonwealth Health system.

headline: Chubb Tempest Re names new Executive Chairman and President in reinsurance leadership shakeup
summary: Chubb elevated James Wixtead to Executive Chairman of its Tempest Re reinsurance business and named Michael O'Donnell President, effective August 1, as part of a broader realignment of Chubb's global reinsurance leadership.

headline: Ascensus to buy AmericanTCS, adding trust, custody and ERISA tech to its retirement platform
summary: Retirement services provider Ascensus agreed to acquire AmericanTCS, gaining trust, custody and ERISA technology tools -- including PensionPro and ERISApedia -- that expand its pooled employer plan and fiduciary services for recordkeepers, banks, insurers and asset managers; the deal is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026.

headline: Court fight over shortened ACA enrollment window heads to appeal
summary: After a judge vacated a federal rule that would have shortened the ACA open enrollment period, HHS appealed the ruling in July, with oral arguments now set for late October as the 2027 marketplace enrollment season approaches.

headline: Ransomware keeps pummeling hospitals even as attacks plateau
summary: Healthcare organizations were hit by ransomware roughly 410 times in the first half of 2026, a slight rise in hospital and clinic attacks even as overall healthcare ransomware growth flattened compared with a surge in attacks on other businesses.

headline: PwC report pegs Singapore and Hong Kong asset pools near $4.5 trillion each
summary: PwC's Asset and Wealth Management Revolution Asia-Pacific report estimates Singapore's assets under management at about $4.6 trillion and Hong Kong's at roughly $4.5 trillion, with regional client assets led by insurance and pension pools.

headline: Marsh, Citi Wealth and Kestra Lead a New Wave of Wealth Management Leadership Hires
summary: A fresh round of executive hires is reshaping wealth management leadership, including Marsh naming a former BlackRock veteran as its U.S. wealth management leader, Citi Wealth hiring a new investments platform experience head, and Kestra Financial naming a new wealth management chief.

headline: Insurers urged to stay cautious on risk assets despite a resilient first half
summary: Invesco's midyear 2026 insurance investment outlook says risk assets have held up well this year, but tight credit spreads, geopolitical risk and inflation uncertainty argue for a cautious stance into the second half.

headline: M&G completes £760 million bulk annuity deal, closing out UK pension scheme's buy-in program
summary: M&G finalized a £760 million bulk purchase annuity with the Smiths Industries Pension Scheme covering more than 10,000 members, the scheme's fifth and final buy-in as UK insurers keep absorbing defined-benefit pension risk.

headline: Startup Carpe debuts a bundled AI intelligence suite aimed at property-casualty claims teams
summary: Carpe launched Carpe Claims, combining case management, computer-vision damage assessment and adjuster oversight tools into one suite, and says its technology is already live at most of the ten largest US P&C carriers.

headline: AdventHealth and Intermountain agree to pool Denver-area hospitals into a joint venture
summary: The two health systems signed a letter of intent to combine five AdventHealth hospitals with three Intermountain facilities in metro Denver, a move that would reshape competition in the Colorado hospital market.

headline: Insurer Genki buys German claims-tech startup Wave Claims
summary: Cologne-based Wave Claims and its Claim OS platform have been acquired by insurer Genki, giving it in-house AI claims-handling technology instead of relying on third-party vendors.

headline: S&P: yield pressure and capital reform push APAC insurers toward private markets
summary: S&P Global Ratings says softening fixed-income yields, regulatory capital reform and macro instability are reshaping investment strategy across Asia-Pacific insurers, with Australian carriers weighing how aggressively to expand beyond traditional asset classes.

headline: Candid Health raises $120M Series D led by Sixth Street, tripling its valuation
summary: Candid Health raised a $120 million Series D led by Sixth Street Growth with participation from Oak HC/FT, 8VC and Y Combinator, tripling its valuation versus its February 2025 Series C as the AI-driven revenue-cycle automation platform reports 190% year-over-year revenue growth.

headline: AllocateRite's model-to-proposal wealthtech platform goes live across RIA firms nationwide
summary: AllocateRite announced its portfolio-modeling and proposal platform is now live across multiple RIA firms, replacing fragmented manual workflows with a single system spanning model construction through client-ready proposals.

headline: Blue Marble and MAPFRE widen access to parametric climate insurance
summary: Parametric insurance specialist Blue Marble partnered with global insurer MAPFRE to expand availability of climate-triggered parametric coverage for communities and businesses exposed to weather-related risks.

headline: AdventHealth and Intermountain Health Plot Denver-Area Hospital Tie-Up
summary: The two health systems signed a letter of intent to affiliate five AdventHealth hospitals with three Intermountain facilities in the Denver metro area. The move is part of a broader wave of regional hospital consolidation this year.

headline: Carlyle and Bain Capital reportedly bid for Wealth Enhancement Group as PE appetite for RIAs intensifies
summary: Private equity interest in large independent wealth managers is heating up, with Carlyle Group and Bain Capital said to be competing for a stake in Wealth Enhancement Group, one of the country's larger RIA aggregators.

headline: Chubb posts stronger underwriting profit in the second quarter as its combined ratio improves
summary: Chubb reported second-quarter 2026 net income of $2.85 billion, with property-casualty net premiums written up 3% and its combined ratio improving to 83.8%, underscoring continued underwriting discipline even as broader industry pricing softens.

headline: Qumis Rolls Out Attorney-Reviewed AI Agents for Reading Commercial Insurance Policies
summary: Chicago insurtech Qumis launched a set of AI agents that produce citation-backed coverage analysis across 16 commercial lines within minutes, letting brokers, carriers, MGAs and TPAs upload full policy programs instead of reviewing them manually.

headline: Horace Mann to acquire two Medical Mutual of Ohio benefits businesses for $240 million
summary: Horace Mann Educators agreed to acquire an employee assistance provider and a supplemental insurer from Medical Mutual of Ohio for about $240 million, adding roughly $200 million in annual revenue and over one million covered lives.

headline: Canopius pulls in HSBC operations veteran as new group COO
summary: Lloyd's insurer Canopius named Stacey Alioto, formerly HSBC's deputy group COO, as its new Group Chief Operating Officer effective September 2026, succeeding the retiring Kate Roy.

headline: Qumis launches attorney-certified AI agents for commercial coverage analysis
summary: Insurtech Qumis rolled out specialist AI agents covering 16 lines of commercial insurance that analyze full programs and produce citation-backed coverage conclusions, already in use at several of the largest US brokers.

headline: Molina's Q2 profit sinks 76% on rising medical costs, guidance still climbs
summary: Molina Healthcare's net income fell sharply in Q2 2026 as its medical loss ratio rose and premium revenue softened, yet the insurer still raised its full-year adjusted earnings guidance.
